“That’s right. And you people didn’t need to observe me. I’m bound by the treaty anyway, so we could not cause hostile interdimensional behavior.”
“What is that so-called treaty? And what is the union?”
He sighed, “Well, the system wouldn’t have taught you that far. It must have informed you of my location since you requested it. Without the explanation, you didn’t need to do so.”
Adam continued his explanation in a tone that was tiresome, “It was still a story far from you people, but to those species that entered the main request and had made some progress, were given time to relax. They questioned what the system really was, and if they could continue the situation with all the dimension giving their all and following their guidance.”
Earth was yet to climb to that level.
“Of course, your kind was still in that state where you were lost in the sweet reward of Mana core and artifacts. It must also be hectic to end the creation of dungeons that lead to collapse continuously. But in a dimension where the main quest was moderately progressed, they start to ponder. To follow the system or to rebel.”
“Rebel?”
“The idea of being kept in the control of the system or find a way to detach yourself from it.”
He talked about what seemed to be a more fundamental concept than the opening and closure of dimensions that could be chosen at the end of the tutorial.
“And the union is an organization that decided that it was right to follow the system for the development of each dimension. They think that they should support as many dimensions as possible to successfully complete the tutorial to get on track of going through the main quest.
“But I didn’t remember Earth receiving such support until now?”
“You must not have noticed, but it was already in progress,” he continued his explanation, “The system primarily protected the dimension that was carrying out the tutorial. The being from another dimension that started the main quest must pay the price to enter a dimension like the Earth. It’s an entrance fee,” he frowned, “I had a similar case. To come here, I paid as much as 1.4 million experience points as an entrance fee to the system! Your expression is getting weird. You must know what this is. Anyways, let us put that explanation away.”
Actually, I was aware of the thing called experience points. I knew the only method to acquire them was in the tutorial stage. The reason why my expression changed was that I was surprised by the ridiculous figure of 1.4 million. Then, I understood the reason for the immortal for roaming around only in the tutorial dimensions.
It was because, when the main quest started, there was a limitation to the movement.
Adam continued to explain, “There’s only one thing that you need to understand. Even an Awakened who finished the tutorial could come to a novice dimension like this for a price. Like me! And most of those were of higher standards than the natives.”
They all should have been equipped with superior battle power that dominates humans. Like Adam, in front of me.
“Among the contents of the treaty, made by the union, there were laws that protect this kind of dimension. And they tend to oversee every dimension… In your kind’s expression, they tend to perform the role of the police. Even those of our dimension that did not join the union forced us to follow by leaning it on our faces. From the victim’s position, it was an act that made them like bullies.” He clicked his tongue a few times and continued, “… Well, that went quite far. Anyway, the union bastards had been observing Earth from the moment that the tutorial had begun, and they’re watching if bastards like me were violating the treaty.”
I could understand. Then why did they let the act of Angelica be? I couldn’t help but question this, “Then why were you participating with Adam Abrams’ identity after paying 1.4 million experience points to come to Earth? Where did the real Adam go?”
He replied bluntly, “When I found the native that I borrowed the name and identity from, He was already dead. The cause was a heart attack.”
He must have inherited his life like a relay baton. Well, rather than inheriting it, it was more like flipping it around.
“And the reason I’m here… if I want to explain it, I must reveal my profession first, though?”
Profession?
He frowned as if it wasn’t easy for him and said, “My profession was… Hmm. There isn’t a suitable word to be compared in your world. But to find something that is remotely close…”
And the following words were something that I had never expected.
“Hmm, yeah. My profession was… a student.”
What?
“And soon I couldn’t Grahhfe$%@st… Ah, you don’t need to bother trying to understand it. It is a pronunciation out of the audible frequency of humans, so it is hard to deliver it as it is,” he contemplated for a while and spoke, “Anyways, to explain in long words in line with your concepts, I would soon have to pass through ‘the second hurdle to prove the knowledge and experience in a certain area of expertise.’ And my major was Pheri#@%@$it.”
He scratched his chin as if it was quite troubling.
“There is no suitable word for this… To describe that, it is ‘a study of research focused on the dungeon monster that appears in each dimension and their anatomical characteristics and behavior, and the change in characteristics of the monsters through the dimensions’.”
“Monster studies? Beast studies?”
“If you translate it that way, the scope becomes too large. The major I had just said is an area of study that focused on specific topics.”
My head was starting to hurt, “Then the reason why you’re here is?”
Was it to do Field Study required for graduation? Should I believe this?

chapters.title: Chapter 83
chapters.content:
Suggestion
I spoke while pressing my temples, “Adam, you… No,” Thinking about it, this wasn’t his real name, “What was your real name?”
“Even if I pronounced it, it was a name that humans wouldn’t be able to hear and follow. Just call me in the current identity, like Adam.”
“Alright, Adam. So, you are….” I couldn’t think straight.
“To speak in a human concept, it means that you’re a student preparing for masters, right? It means that you’re a graduate student.”
“You insult me with such a comparison….!” Adam showed that he was appalled with his expression and tone.
“But you just said your profession was a student.”
“This was why the mechanical translation of the words that ignore the cultural background led to a misunderstanding! The profession of a student in our world was completely different from that of Earth. And the hurdle that I’m preparing for wasn’t as simple a process as you ….”
Before he went on and on with his explanation, I was all ears for a while, but it didn’t feel very sensible. I reached out my hand and stopped him, “Okay, okay. And the purpose of your stay on Earth was to gather samples of monsters?”
When I was tracing his steps, I saw the scene of him carefully gutting various monsters and storing them. I was wondering for what reason he was taking them. Was it for research purposes?
“Yes. I need a dungeon monster connected to a dimension in an early tutorial stage.”
He said that he came to North Korea after leaving the official activity scene to collect various samples from a region that Breaks continually happened.
‘For sure, for that condition, this would be the ideal place.’
A location where he didn’t have to be appeared.
‘…but he’s just a student?’
A being whose profession was in studying and research received an SSS-Rank when he came over to Earth, and he was equipped with superior battle power incomparable to humans. He also had a strange skill that didn’t require Mana usage. Were all of the species in the tutorial beasts like him?
“Well, have you asked everything that you were curious about me? Now, it’s my turn to ask.”
Expectations glowed from his eyes. He asked as if he couldn’t hold it back anymore, “That item, where was the dungeon that you found the [Door of Hope]?”
I explained the path that led me to acquire the ring, and I informed him that the gate connected to that dungeon had already been closed. And as I did so, Adam’s face soon distorted with disappointment.
“What, it’s not an acquisition, but it’s an additional reward?”
The acquisition meant the things that lay around dungeons like the devil’s sword, and additional rewards meant that it was acquired from the choices that the system gives after the Clear.
Adam sighed, “You picked this among the random rewards? You’re one lucky guy.”
I asked, “Does it matter if this was a dungeon acquisition?”
“Of course, it does! It means that part of the Sebrarian empire was used as a material to compose the middle dimension where the dungeon was!”
Sebrarian Empire? Those words were mentioned again. I spoke about the fact that I inferred from the item descriptions, “That thing, I don’t know which dimension did the country exist in, but didn’t it fall apart ages ago?”
“You know about it well, don’t you? But since the middle dimension itself was of dimensions that transcends time and space… so the period didn’t matter.”
What I didn’t know about here was that it was a combination that even transcended time, “It combines the space of different points in time, you said?”
“Yeah, the reason why the monsters that have a certain level of civilization, and differ in clothing and weapons, depending on the dungeons, was that the dimension or the point in time it was taken from might be different.” He returned to the original topic and asked about the internal environment of Siheung 8 Dungeon. It was the information discussed in detail among the media, but seeing that he seemed to be unaware, he must have been here for a long time.
He clicked his tongue after listening to my answer, “Apart from the portal, wasn’t it an environment without a trace of civilization?”
Indeed, it was. The fact that there were many floating wastelands in the air and covered with thick fog was interesting, but it was more like a natural environment that wasn’t affected by the touch of civilization.
“It would be meaningless to go there myself now.”
As I was listening, I got curious, “Are you looking for a trace of the Sebrarian empire?”
“Of course!”
He was excited after seeing my ring because he expected it to be an acquisition. He was excited at the hope that the field in the dungeon was an old downtown of the Sebrarian empire and that he could find more items relating to the empire.
“Those artifacts are separately categorized with the name of ‘Empirical Heritage.’ Most species that finished the tutorial are frantically looking for it!”
What was such a meaningful thing? He explained with much more enthusiasm. Every item that mentioned the empire was more valuable than those of the same value. Those items caused an interdimensional war!
‘Wait, I have five of those on me.’
Adam identified the [Door of Hope], which was the ring I had equipped, but I didn’t think he had noticed the [Stardust Wing] absorbed in my body—seeing that he hadn’t mentioned it yet. Apart from the two I had equipped, I have three more, including [The 3rd Class Imperial Guard Program] that I gave to Nate. These items contained the keywords of the empire.
‘It was the right choice to put those conditions in the deal with the Spirit.’
I asked him, thinking that I should attempt something similar next time I have another chance to deal with the spirit, “Then do you plan to stay here and continue hunting monsters?”
For the pure purposes of collection and research, He’d never done anything significant in my previous life, apart from disappearing. It bothered me that he threatened to slaughter the refugees a while ago, but I had caused the situation by stalking him.
He replied in a relaxed tone, “Hmm, well, I was thinking about getting back to my original world within this year since I’m almost done with analyzing patterns over here.”
It was not much different from the time when his traces completely disappeared in my previous life.
‘Rather than the possibility of something happening after he met Angelica in the future, did he depart because it was about time?’
It may only have been that their timings overlapped. But then, “······Yeah, I was going to.” There was a strange light hovering around his eyes that bothered me, “By the way, I’m sure I’ve never seen your face before when I was going along with the human race. If you had your whole body plastered with SS-Class, and you had got the [Door of Hope] as a reward, you’d definitely be on the top of the list in this dimension, but how do I not know? It hasn’t even been a few months since I buried myself in this land.”
Clearly, the pace at which I grew was extremely rapid, and it hadn’t been long since the global media began to deal with me. Most of the cases that made me known would have happened while Adam was wandering in old North Korean soil.
“Hmm,” The eyes looking at me were full of interest, “Let’s check you out.”
Swwash!
The air broke apart, and a Hunter-exclusive terminal popped out. Since this was near Fortress City, it wouldn’t be too hard to catch the signal. Quickly after manipulating the device, he seemed to have found something.
“Oh, here it is! There have been so many articles in the past few days it’s not hard to find about you,” he laughed with his teeth revealed, “That’s exactly the same face behind the mask,”
When he floated the hologram in the air, my face came up in a big frame with the newspaper article. He quickly read the article with his hand on his chin. Then he tilted his head, “It’s weird. This is too weird. You have achieved this much in less than half a year?” He stared at me as if he were observing me, “I’d understand if you were of a species of another world pretending to be human like me. But it’s not that either,” His eyes grew bigger, “Literally, it means that you’re a genius!”
It was hard to keep up with the suddenly changed topic of the conversation. He, who even figured out my name through the Internet, grinned and said, “Hey, you. Seo Jin-Wook!” He must have reached some kind of conclusion by running some calculations in his head, but I couldn’t guess what it was, “You said it yourself, didn’t you? If we need something from each other, we’ll be able to make a deal.”
His comment made me frown my eyebrows. What more was he planning to talk about?
“Listen, it’s not a losing proposition for either of us,” he raised his finger and pointed at me, “Looking at the fact that you’ve been dealing with the system to buy my location information, you’re in a place to actively jump into and intervene in the tutorial quest, aren’t you? I don’t know if the motive was the heroism to save the Earth by weeding off spies or a personal reason that I’m not aware of. Anyway, an enthusiastic attitude is important. If you stand out this much, you’ll soon be ‘chosen’ by the system. You still don’t understand the meaning, do you?”
Actually, I knew it very well…. and even the selection had already been completed. There was only one person on the planet who’d been selected, which was me.
“Looking at your equipment, the gap is too far with other people on Earth. It will be hard to narrow down in the future, too. Also, since you received an SS-Rank, you must have over 30,000 Active Mana, right? That’s enough for you to be in the lead in the starting line.”
He said with shining eyes, “Well, here’s my offer. I have a lot of useful information for you! You just asked me about the Sebrarian Empire, didn’t you? Don’t you want to hear more details about it?”
He was quick-witted, that’s for sure.
“Other than that, my head was full of useful information for beings in the tutorial dimension! Doesn’t it interest you?”
It indeed was tempting. Instead of expressing my interest with a reaction or accepting it right away, I waited for an explanation that would follow.
Adam pulled his lips to smile, “You may think highly of yourself since you’re ahead of everyone else in the world called Earth, right? You may even wonder if you need help from an alien like me. However, it is better not to let your guard down too quickly. Your kind has no idea. The tutorial quest was literally just a tutorial!”
In my previous life, I died before we got to finish the tutorial quest. After completing the tutorial in this life, I only have a general idea of what would happen afterward and what the situation of the Earth was going to be like.
“At the end of the tutorial, all the handicaps imposed by the system that protects the Earth are gone. More gates will be opened, and dungeon boundaries will often collide. To make things even worse, in a situation with more contacts with other beings from other worlds, the entrance fee disappears!”
This meant that even those who were working on the main quest were free to come and go.
“This dimension belongs to the beginning of the tutorial. Even contact with other dimensions in the tutorial doesn’t happen properly. But then, what if there was an advisor who can help you the best in this situation.”
I knew what he’s trying to say…
“Yes, I’m going to be your information consultant!”
If it was about a dimension in the same level of standard, being in the tutorial stage, I knew a lot about them due to my previous life. However, the information on the main quest was entirely different. Only that, listening to his story, two things were bothering me. The more suggestions he made, the more thorough I needed to look behind them.
“Isn’t it against the Union’s treaty? An act of interfering in this dimension and spilling information at will.”
“They don’t particularly forbid it. In fact, only a few voluntarily come here to this kind of novice dimension like me. There’s only so much you can get. The resources and labor that can be mined in this world are meaningless to us.”
Even in the former European powers, where the difference in technology was apparent, underground resources, mined from other continents and slaves, were attractive resources. However, if the difference was too broad, it was natural that the desire to touch disappeared.
“Then why do you volunteer to offer me such?”
“That’s because, of course, you’re special!”
“Because I’m growing fast?”
“It’s not just fast; it’s overwhelming compared to other beings!”
There seemed to be no doubt in his mind that I would not be an alien like him. It was a firm conviction from the way he was speaking.
“Once again, you will definitely be chosen by the system in a few years.”
He began explaining the screening quests. I knew everything about them, but I listened quietly. Special trials were given only to a few Awakened individuals selected by the system. If you overcame them, you would be given an intangible credit of ‘experience points’.’ You could exchange them for items that could directly affect the tutorial quest or change them to other tangible or intangible rewards.
“The only way to get experience points at the tutorial stage is through screening quests!”
He followed by saying that both the tutorial’s experience points and the main quest’s experience points had the same value. Also, after entering the main quest, you needed a lot of experience points for reasons.
“I’ll be an information consultant for you, so you can hand me some of the experience points you’ll get in return!”
“No, wait, that doesn’t make sense,” I pointed out a hidden flaw in his words, “Do you think I’m going to hand them over to you when you’ve stressed the importance of experience points?”
“Listen. I think you’ll monopolize most of the points you can get at the tutorial stage!”
It was an almost accurate prediction, ‘I’m not going to take most of them, but I’m going to take them all. That’s the plan for now.’
He continued, “And there must be a limit to the experience point that one can use in the tutorial stage. There will be a remainder even if you use the points to proceed with the tutorial and things you need personally. This is why the system created the concept of ‘point transfer.’ If you hand over the remaining points to me and get equally valuable information, it’s a win-win deal for both of us.”
While he spoke so enthusiastically, raising his voice, I was quickly searching my memory, comparing the total experience points earned by all hunters in my previous life with the points needed to be consumed to actually proceed with the tutorial. Also, I added up all of the point consumption options that were irrelevant to the tutorial process.
‘Certainly, that makes sense. Some screening quests couldn’t be cleared in the past life, so considering all the rewards.’
Points will remain. When I was seriously considering his proposal, Adam’s expression distorted at the same time.
Swwash.
Our gaze pointed to one place in unison, and our eyes were fixated. Someone was approaching over the horizon.
‘What was that? We’re in the middle of an important conversation!’
The man broke through the dust of the wilderness and led dozens of men behind him.
‘Seo Do-Hyung!’
It was an A-Rank hunter who was wanted in South Korea. The Awakened, who must have proudly been among the runaways who were mostly composed of D and E-Rank.
“Are you the guys? I don’t know where you guys are from, but you messed with the wrong people today!”
After gathering the Awakened in the trusteeship region and turning it into a criminal organization and starting with human trafficking by selling the refugees abroad, they later even distributed drugs into the Fortress City and got caught. And they were pieces of trash that would immediately be executed on the scene after being arrested by the U.N. military that cooperated with the International Hunter Union.
The man, who would die within a year even if left alone, giggled and said, “I’ll kill you both here!”
The moment I heard it, my irritation exploded. Adam also clenched his teeth so tightly that his molars threatened to crumble, “Of course, he doesn’t know any of us.”
I was wearing a slime mask, and Adam disguised his face as he could transform other parts of his body and couldn’t be identified by him. He must have thought we weren’t much of a hunter because he didn’t know our faces.
“Hearing from my men, you two seem to be about B-Rank. Did you think that you can do as you wish if you came all the way here? It’s a mistake. Do you know who I am? I am a man who is supposed to receive S-Rank….”
At that moment, Adam and I yelled in unison.
“Shut up!”
“Fuck off!”
When my sword energy exploded, Adam’s right hand turned into a long whip and rushed towards him.
Shhhhhh!
Boo-boo-boom!
“Ahhhhhhhh!”
“What, what, what!”
After a while, when the dust had settled, at the place where Seo Do-hyung stood, the remains of the man who had turned into a lump of blood and flesh remained.
“Ehh…. Eh…. Aaaaaaaargh!” Only then did the remaining men start to run away in confusion.
“Now, then,” Adam, who recovered his arm that had turned into a red whip, spoke to me with a peaceful expression and a tone that seemed like nothing ever happened.
“That’s all I have to offer. What do you think?”

chapters.title: Chapter 84
chapters.content:
Introduce
I eventually accepted Adam’s offer. The details on how the duration of cooperation would be, how many experience points should be shared, and other things were agreed to be decided later on. For now, he expressed his intention to follow me for now.
“The point is important, but I have an interest in Awakened, such as you. You’re a research-worthy subject.”
“What? You said you were planning to return home. Can you extend it like this as you wish?”
“It doesn’t matter.”
“Won’t the advising professor come after you? Since the graduate student, who was supposed to assist him or her run away. Perhaps, is this avoidance of graduation?”
“I’m not a graduate student!” he negated with annoyance and murmured, “And, why do I assist them? They should assist me.”
Anyways, there seemed to be no problem on the part of him extending his stay on Earth. I had contacted Secretary Kim beforehand, and his quarters were prepared in the office house. A few days later, by the request of Adam, who said that he hated dealing with bothersome things, sneaked us into the house by activating [Stealth]. It was because the reporters that arrived before us had crowded the place like a wall of men.
‘Well, it is indeed newsworthy.’
In my announcement that I would import a foreign SSS-Rank hunter to South Korea and that I would sign him up to the guild, the Hunter Management Department reacted enthusiastically. To accommodate the two of us, they were ready to send a private jet and lay a red carpet on the military airport. Today, as we arrived in the country, the government gave their best to disperse the information to the media. It was a speed that the Celestial Dragon PR team should learn from.
“I have arrived.”
Secretary Kim, who was waiting for me, bowed, “Welcome, Guild Master,” Joyfully, a smile hung on his lips. His gaze moved to Adam, who was beside me, “You brought back a very large present.”
“This man, he knows how to speak Korean.”
“Eh, really?”
It wasn’t even translation magic, and I don’t know how he did it, but for now, Abrams said he could speak most of the language that exists on Earth. Secretary Kim said while looking at him admiringly, at the body of almost 3 meters in height that had the muscle mass beyond human limits, “It’s nice to meet you, I’m Kim Byeong-Ho. You can call me Secretary Kim, for convenience.”
“It’s a pleasure.”
Secretary Kim led us to the room that Adam would use.
“We prepared every piece of furniture by specially having it made.”
The unique furniture, adjusted to the size of the 3-meter giant, was perfectly prepared in the room. I didn’t expect that it would be this prepared in that short time.
‘Anyways, he’s really good at his job.’
I said while facing Secretary Kim, “You’ve worked hard.”
“It’s nothing. Actually, we did newly prepare the furniture, the house structure may be somewhat uncomfortable to Mr. Abrams, so I was thinking of building a new building that extends to the house.
Indeed, considering the height of the ceiling and the entrance, that would seem better.
“Proceed with it as you wish.”
“Alright, understood.”
Adam could change his body to a smaller state than he was right now if necessary, but it was not only uncomfortable; if he maintained that state, it applied too much pressure on the ‘things’ that were inside him right now. Due to those reasons, he was maintaining a larger body compared to regular humans.
“How about Nate and Hibiki?”
“They’re in the basement training room.”
The two of them had left the accommodation and transferred here after I inaugurated as the Guild Master. After I opened the door, their gazes fixed on me.
“Jin-Wook!” Nate joyfully exclaimed, while running towards me, “You have arrived?”
Hibiki calmly greeted us.
“Hmm? How much heritage do you really own?” It was Adam who said that, seeing the tattoo on Nate’s neck as he came in. Of course, he recognized it in a glance.
“I do have a few.”
The female being connected with the tattoo, shaped of blue Mana, floated on top of Nate’s head. The spirit glanced at me indifferently then took it back.
The artificial intelligence, which kept its silence if nothing serious was going on, was also an item related to the Sebrarian Empire.
“Then, let’s introduce one another.”
I introduced them to each other. Nate, who was looking at the overwhelmingly sized giant with his jaw dropped, and Hibiki, who showed a slightly wavering gaze, as she realized his identity of that of an SSS-Ranked hunter.
“I was observing you from outside. Looking at how you use your skill, Hibiki, I think you’ll need another promotion review soon, right?”
A slight flush appeared on her cheeks. Hibiki’s active Mana had already increased to an A-Rank state. The light of the core proved that she had given her best effort as her life depended on it.
At that moment, Nate butted in, “Jin-Wook! I learned to do a new thing in the meanwhile!” he opened his palm as if to show off. Then, after a little hesitation, “You said Mr. Adam is also an Awakened, right? He’s not normal, right?”
There is only one reason why he asks that.
“Yes, that’s right.”
“Then, now! Look at this!”
Swish!
A wind blew. In his shadows, a zombified orc sprung out of it.
“Hmm?!”
Then for the first time, Adam showed keen interest in the others being apart from me.
“Undead?”
Nate said enthusiastically, “If I were to explain how this works.”
As he rolled his eyes and looked at Hibiki, she snapped back with a loathing expression, unusually of her, “You try sending me that one more time! I’ll really kill you!”
Clearly, there had been confrontations while I was gone. They must have gotten that close to exchange those kinds of words to each other.
Anyways, ‘sending,’ was it? Comparing it to the memory of the past life, I understood what Nate was trying to do.
‘Ah, that one.’
On Hibiki’s strong reaction, Nate grumbled with a pouted mouth, “What a fuss, I’ve only pranked her once,” He turned his head and looked at me, “Now, look at this!”
Swish! A wind blew once again. The form of the Orc swayed like smoke and disappeared in an instant. And instead of Nate’s shadow swallowing it this time.
“It’s in my shadow?” I said while looking at the floor.
“What, you’re not surprised?” Nate scratched his head as if his excitement didn’t live up to his expectations.
Did I not react enough? Well, I’d already seen it in the past life, so I said, “Its senses are connected in this state, right?”
“Yes. Even if the Orc is inside the shadow, it can vaguely see the situation outside and hear. If I want, I can observe and listen as well.”
“And you can take it out of the shadow if you want?”
“Of course!”
It was obvious what kind of prank he pulled off on Hibiki with this.
“Taking advantage of the gap that she was focused on training [Multiple Cognition], you placed a zombie inside her shadow?”
“Woah, you know me really well!”
The zombie Orc was hidden in Hibiki’s shadow, in that state, and aiming for a window of opportunity when she went to the 2nd floor after finishing her practice, it had extended its half-decayed arm from the floor and grabbed Hibiki’s ankle hard, or so he said. Of course, Hibiki was very surprised.
“That’s why the windows and the internal materials of the second floor had been redone.
“I’m sorry.”
“That’s alright. To retaliate with magic by a reflex means that you’re trained that well.”
Because of the spell she poured out towards the zombie, the second floor was destroyed and needed a general repair.
I said to Nate, “But then, wouldn’t it be better to upgrade than to be satisfied in this state?”
He tilted his head, “How?”
“For now, you need the process of taking out a zombie then putting it back into another’s shadow. The path that it moves can be seen by normal people as well.”
“Well, Hibiki didn’t see it.”
She protested, “That was because I was concentrating!”
I nodded and said, “That’s right. But what if you develop a way that you can stealthily move the undead that nobody can notice them going into his or her shadow even if their eyes are wide open?”
Then Hibiki looked at me with a gaze full of betrayal. I protested with my hand.
“No, I didn’t mean it to be used to prank Hibiki but for actual situations. I think that it would increase its utility. How about in that way?” I say it like I just came up with this idea, “Nate, you’ll overlap your shadow with the opponents. In that state, shouldn’t your subordinate be able to move from your shadow to the others? Without having to reveal itself directly, that is,” And I added on to it, “Of course, I don’t know if it can work. I just thought that it could be an idea.”
Of course, it worked since it was a method used in the previous life.
“Huh? Somehow, I think that would work?!” Nate exclaimed with joy. Instead of moving his own body, he tilted his shadow itself a bit and overlapped with mine. He seemed to concentrate by frowning. And after some time had passed, “…. Hmm, it doesn’t work just yet. But I think it would work after some practice!”
It must be that his mastery was still low for it to be done, but it was only a matter of time. On the other hand, Hibiki made an expression like she was hating the parent and making an uncontrollable kid into a dangerous toy.
I added a few words for her, “And no more pranks on guild members.”
“Alright!” Just now, there seemed to be an awkward pause before he answered.
“Hmm.”
Adam, who was listening to our conversation interestingly until then, suddenly butted in, “Hey, you. You’re name’s Nate, right?”
With his shining eyes, he looked at Adam, “Yes?”
“The undead just now, wouldn’t you mind handing a few of them to me? It’s my first time seeing this kind of skill. I’m curious about the method they use to move. I want to perform some experiments on them.”
Was Nate’s unique skill a strange concept to Adam as well?
“Hmm. Well, it’s not impossible. There are lots of Orcs.”
Apart from Nate’s zombies categorizes as ‘friends,’ I think he didn’t have much attachment to undeads that he labeled as ‘subordinates.’ Even so, as he must have some hostile feelings to the words of the experiment, he hesitated to answer.
As if he misunderstood his reaction, Adam said, “Of course, not for free.”
The more I looked at him; I felt he was an alien that was very sensitive to mutual respect. Adam pondered for a while and transformed his right hand. The flesh became covered with red muscles and inflated to soon sprout up to about his kidney’s size. On the tip of his transformed hand revealed a nail in the form of a sharp sickle.
“Woah!” Nate looks at his arms with a bummed face.
“This is from upgrading the Giant Mantis’ front leg.”
What he mentioned was a powerful monster that came out in S-Class dungeons as a boss monster.
Nate shouted with glowing eyes, “No way, that’s super cool!”
Hibiki and I both said in a tone that it is incomprehensible in unison, “…Cool?”
Adam smiled and said, “If you want, I’ll transform your right hand like this. I have the material that is equivalent to a human arm just at the right…”
Nate raised his hand even before he could finish his words, “I want to do it! I’ll do it!”
“Hey, wait,” I had to intervene, “Explain to me how the modification works to me as well. And Nate, how can you accept it right away when someone offers you to transform your body like that!”
“Ah, right. I don’t like anything that hurts.”
Adam assured that he shouldn’t worry about it, “You won’t feel a thing,”
“Really?”
The alien continued as if to entice Nate, “In this nail, you can even store Mana in it. That means that it is equivalent to an artifact. Depending on how you use it, you can even win over an S-Class item…”
As if to react to what he said, the moment Adam injected Mana into the Giant Mantis’ claws, spontaneous telepathy resonated in the room.
– A danger element found against the protection subject!
The source of the mind wave was the blue spirit floating on top of Nate’s head.
“Again!”
Hibiki freaked out and unfolded protection magic. Nate also frowned and shouted at the spirit.
“Hey, you stupid…!”
At then, Swish!v A light flashed in the air, then a giant metal structure was summoned.
It was of a scale that would fill up the training room and the theater’s size. As if it were fixated in the air, the thing that floated was a large-caliber multi-round cannon that could shoot a thousand rounds of bullets at once. Once again, telepathy resonates.
– Warning! Warning! No further access is allowed. It would be responded with immediate firing in case of non-response…
I dispiritedly murmured, “… At least it doesn’t shoot right away this time, so it has learned something.”
Nate snapped back at the spirit on top of his head, “Hey, you stupid! How does this look like a dangerous situation!”
Adam, who was watching this mess, scratched his cheeks, “This is why this item was avoided. There are rare artifacts treated that way among the Imperial Heritages.”
He continued his words, having everyone’s attention, “The Empire shared knowledge and experience by connecting to the intellectual group network when it was on its high. Artificial intelligence controlled it like a baby. It’s not only bothersome for one to educate the concepts and objects one by one, but the protection is also programmed to be carried out first rather than processing other commands. It doesn’t abide by order of the master that well, and crucially, it’s an attribute item, so it can’t be traded; such a shitty…”
Nate looked at me with eyes full of betrayal.

chapters.title: Chapter 85
chapters.content:
Moths (1)
Grand Croix’s Guild Master, Kim Kyung-Rok, was screaming at his phone, “Does that make sense? Even if the CCTV at the spot where they’d found Ji-Hoon’s car was not working, what about other CCTVs? Were there really no traces found?!”
He talked about Kim Ji-Hoon, who was his brother and the only other S-Rank hunter in the guild, who went missing not long ago.
“I’m sorry. I’ve been keeping track of the situation through the police and the Hunter Department sources,” the guild member on the phone spoke with a dark tone, “They said that they really couldn’t find anything. Like as if he evaporated on the spot ···.”
Kim Kyung-Rok felt like his head was going to explode, and he was going to collapse.
‘The scene was clean with no sign of battle!’
Common sense suggested it was normal for people to leave even a small trace of being killed or kidnapped. Since there were none, it meant that an S-class hunter was one-sidedly attacked and failed to respond. Kim Kyung-Rok hung up the phone and continued to think while steaming with anger.
‘It’s possible with a large group of A-level Hunters, but no large crew can move cleanly without a trace like this. The opponent was definitely few in numbers. If they handled an S-Rank with only a few of them, it meant that at least an S or of a higher rank hunter is mixed in.’
No matter how hard he thought about it, only a limited number of suspects had the ability and motive to meet all these conditions. Kim Kyung-Rok gritted his teeth and muttered.
“For sure, this is an act by the Celestial Dragons, those bastards!”
It was clear that the Guild Master, Seo Jin-Wook, must have been involved.
“He took revenge for the trouble during the promotion review!”
In reality, it happened because Kim Ji-Hoon first taunted and even threatened his life. After his leg recovered, Kim Ji-Hoon himself rather publicly spoke that he would retaliate. To weigh the fault, his brother was obviously more guilty, but that was not important to Kim Kyung-Rok right now.
“Damn it; they have a clear suspect, and what is that bullshit that they can’t investigate!”
Grand Croix’s opinion, which pointed out Celestial Dragon as the culprit and demanded a thorough investigation, was silenced. In addition to the lack of evidence, Celestial Dragon’s top hunters, including Seo Jin-Wook, had a perfect alibi on the day.
“Yeah, it’s not a situation where we can rely on the public power anyway.”
For some time now, the government has blatantly been lenient to Celestial Dragon and Seo Jin-Wook. There have been complaints that it was discrimination against other guilds, but nothing had changed other than asking for some understanding.
“This leaves us no choice but for the Grand Croix to take revenge for ourselves!”
Kim Kyung-Rok’s heart was filled with deep feelings of loss and anger due to his blood-relative disappearance. Simultaneously, in his head, he was quickly judging and calculating the situation as a Guild Master.
“If this situation continues, Grand Croix will be overpowered by Celestial Dragon.”
His younger brother was both a precious blood relative and one of the hunters that represented the guild.
“Before it’s too late…”
Both the public and Awakened had already begun to recognize Celestial Dragon as the nation’s No. 1 guild. A critical move to flip the situation was needed. As Kim Kyung-Rok was desperately thinking about ways to grab both revenge and benefit into his hands, a voice called.
“Guild Master!” The door to the office opened, and a guild member rushed in.
“What is it?!”
“I think you should check the n-news!”
He quickly opened the hologram as if there was no room for further explanation. The news screen, which was being carried on as an emergency breaking news, filled the space.
– …As for that, neither the Celestial Dragon Guild nor Adam Abrams himself disclosed further explanation. Meanwhile, the British government has sent a formal letter of protest through its diplomatic channel, saying that no prior arrangements were made, and has expressed their position to sue them with unlawful exportation of hunters to the International Hunter Union. However, the precedent suggested no way to force the parties on both Adam Abrams and the Celestial Dragon Guild. Also…
Kim Kyung-Rok’s face became blank, ‘What were they talking about?’ The announcer’s words made their way to his ears, but the meaning did not properly settle in his head. Two phrases that reminded him of another were mentioned along with the news.
Adam Abrams, a British SSS-Rank hunter with the Celestial Dragon Guild of Korea.
Dumbfounded, he murmured, “What? Why were they on the same news?”
And the moment the announcer’s face disappeared in the hologram, and the photos of the Guild Master Seo Jin-Wook and Adam Abrams appeared as the reference data.
As the subtitles changed, unbelievable sentences were reflected in Kim Kyung-Rok’s eyes.
– Breaking news! Adam Abrams, a British SSS-Rank hunter, joins the Celestial Dragon Guild!
– Celestial Dragon; will become a large-scale international guild beyond being the no. 1 in Korea?
As Kim Kyung-Rok finally grasped the totality of the situation, his temples’ veins were protruding.
He shouted as if he had lost his mind, “What does this make sense?!” The following words were close to screaming, “Why does Adam Abrams sign up for Celestial Dragon right now?”
Clink!
Something flew, and the bulletproof window of the Grand Croix guild room was broken. It was already the second time that week.
*
I showed Adam the hologram after we moved to another place. Based on the system’s location information, the satellite image was taken by contracting with a company.
“This is the list that I have secured. Awakened from dimensions that were done with the tutorial.”
Adam whistled in admiration, “You got the Awakened location information without using a single point?”
Experience points were usually used to get this from the system in the first place, but he was amazed that I took care of this just with my words.
“How much did you overachieve to get this much reward? What have you done?”
I’d changed my words. I spoke while pointing at the pictures wherein most of them were camouflaged to seem familiar to humans.
“Anyway, do you know any being among them?”
I’d put the attempt to stalk the rest of the ones on the list without any good plans on hold. I thought, waiting for Adam’s reaction, ‘Adam noticed me even when I amplified the SS-class [Stealth] with an item. Other species might also be able to identify me in a way that I’m not aware of. I should avoid following them too close without knowing what they’re capable of.’
It was a lesson I learned from this incident. However, it wa not possible to leave them as they were when the list was in hand, so I was trying to get information through Adam.
He looked carefully at the picture on the map and said, “First of all, this guy, this guy, and this guy, and… oh, this guy.”
He quickly picked up six pictures from the map and the list, “Don’t touch these guys as much as possible. They’re 100% harmless to your world, so get your hands off them. Don’t follow them like you tried on me. Playing with the spark will turn into a wildfire.”
“Why?”
“These were the ‘eyes’ that the Union has planted on Earth,” He continued the explanation, “I didn’t know their fake identities. I get to find out through an unexpected path, huh. I see a pattern. Seeing that they’re arranged this way, it’s for sure.”
“When you say eyes, you mean that they were the watchers from the Union, right?”
Come to think of it, the position of the six was not concentrated at any point. They were scattered all over the globe at a certain distance. As if they were to divide this star into six zones and be responsible for each of them.
I remembered what the ministry spirit said.
– Based on their behavioral patterns, some were believed to have been dispatched with a mission as an observer.
‘That’s what it meant!’
Adam said, nodding his head, “Then, except for the six I picked, it meant that the rest of them were the problem.”
For a long time, those who stayed in this world, even when they were not aliens, were dispatched from the Union.
“There were no obvious characteristics like the eyes, so I didn’t know who they were from this point of view. They should have had their own reasons, just as I was here for a special reason.”
He turned his head and asked me, “Do you have any more detailed information about the alien you’re looking for?”
I did not tell Adam the details but only informed him that I was looking for a particular alien who had long been hiding on Earth. I recalled the man’s ability from Seo Gyu-Cheol’s memory. Besides the unique skill of [Mercardius’ Seed], there were many other peculiar abilities. For example, the ability to perfectly read Seo Gyu-Cheol’s thoughts without coming into contact with him and modify Seo Gyu-Cheol’s personality and completely erase his paternal love. Other abilities included being able to return Seo Gyu-Cheol’s body and the ability to give Seo Gyu-Cheol 10,000 potential Mana that could be activated within a day.
Adam’s face gradually distorted when he heard my explanation, “Hey, that thing. Were you sure it’s a mortal?”
“Have you never heard of it?”
“It’s mostly unfamiliar, and the effects are tremendous,” He thought about it for a while and said, “Something about it, it smells very dangerous.”
Was he saying that it was out of the ordinary even by the world’s standards where the tutorial had been completed?
“Let’s say everything else is as it is, but he can give someone potential Mana To say that is the capability of a mortal, it is rather…” He said in a low voice, “It’s almost like something that only the ‘system’ can handle.”
No way, it can’t be. Adam pondered and told me, “This is interesting to me, too. I’ll gather information from my original dimension as well.”
“Thanks. Anyway, you’re saying that there’s a mix of dangerous beings on this list, right?”
He looked at the hologram with a different glance, “Hey, one piece of advice is…”
“Yes, I’m not going to stalk them.”
“I’d recommend that, too. It won’t be too late to decide after receiving a reply from our world. We don’t know what other hidden abilities our opponent may have.”
Then, he suddenly raised his voice, “If I barely had built a partnership with you and you die, I’ll be wasting my time and lose my point! It’s a no-no for you to die that sad.”
“I’m grateful, thank you.”
*
After that, Adam was leisurely lying around at home, waiting for me to receive a screening quest. I deliberately didn’t inform him that I was already selected. Screening quests were fluid trials in which content is changed in real-time and was linked to each other. To make the first step perfect, I decided to start the first quest to complete the upcoming historic event. Anyway, it was a quest that other people would only be able to access after a few years, So I didn’t worry about anyone else stealing it away from me. However, I lied because I had to explain the fact that I knew the future to justify such an explanation.
‘Since it’s a difference of little time anyway.’
When the future event I remember took place, I planned to say that I received the screening quest and then proceeded with the Clear. On the other hand, Adam’s life as an unemployed man unintentionally ended early because of me.
– Breaking news! It’s the update that the Celestial Dragon Guild’s Gate Search Team had found another gate again in Jeonnam. It’s already the 7th gate they had found by the guild this month. They were discovering new gates at a truly phenomenal pace.
The search team was expanded and reorganized and consisted of support-type Awakened, locally and internationally. They dug up the gates as if they were pointing out the water veins all over the country.
“Hmm? What. There were such monsters? I’ll be right back; I will be going there for a while.”
Some monsters got Adam interested, as were found suddenly, and if he saw such a thing, he went on a single-person mission. When he finished collecting samples, he also Cleared them. Such behavior only made Celestial Dragon’s evaluation go up further. Of course, the guild’s public relations team quickly arranged to satisfy and manipulate public opinion.
“The Celestial Dragon Guild sends an SSS-Rank hunter even to a C-Class dungeon!”
It was only because the type of monsters was important to him regardless of the Class of dungeons, but the public did not know this motivation.
“If they use their human resources like that, it would balance their profit.”
“They’re stating that safety of the people is more important than profit!”
“But isn’t the Celestial Dragon Search Team amazing too? They find a gate almost every day!”
“They mean to say that there is no business that could win over numbers. Has there ever been a guild that’s focused so much Hunter on the gate search? Most of them were busy mining cores in dungeons that had already been discovered.”
Obviously, if one could discover the gates well because of the number of people poured on the workforce, all the guilds would have done so. The real secret lay in the fact that I led the search to the right place, but those circumstances were unknown to the public. The public and the media were enthusiastic about the Celestial Dragon, who found the gates at a pace that could not be compared to the past. This excitement led to criticism of questioning the competence of what other guilds had done before.
It was pointed out that if they had invested in the workforce to the extent that the Celestial Dragon was doing now, they would have found more gates and lowered the risk of breaks. On the other hand, some seemed to have noticed that the Celestial Dragon’s momentum was clearly abnormal.
*
“Hmm?” Adam, who was talking to me in the room, suddenly turned his head. He didn’t use any skills, but he noticed someone’s approach.
“Oh, it’s him again.”
I could tell who he was talking about by unfolding the [Penetration] along the direction he was looking at.
“Woah, he’s hardworking. He checked in today as well.”
Back then, suspicious signs had often been seen around the guild building and my home office. First of all, envoys secretly sent from governments, hunter agencies, and foreign guilds offered me naturalization, offering various conditions. There was also a proposal to merge one’s country’s guild with Celestial Dragon, promising massive compensation. Of course, I didn’t even pretend to hear it.
‘I already have much money to the point that it might start rotting, and it’s most important that I can move freely in the first place.’
When there was no response, the spy that rushed in with another intention caught my eyes afterward. The unprecedented moves and achievements that Celestial Dragon had recently shown, meant that some were trying to dig up the secret hidden behind them. Among them was the man who was hovering around this house in disguise today as well.
I said leisurely, “He’ll probably cross the fence tonight.”
“How do you know?”
“Nate’s already sneaked one of his subordinates into his shadows.”
“Ahhhh,” Adam nodded.
*
That night, Seo Jin-Wook predicted the presence of an intruder. As expected, a man broke through the barrier and entered the house in the middle of darkness. The internal structure had already been completely identified through scouting and clairvoyance. The man hid by activating the highest ranked [Stealth] skill he could were used to help him not be discovered even though they were all over the house.
‘Here it is, the office in the house.’
The man’s goal was to identify the clues of the secret hidden by Seo Jin-Wook, the Guild Master of Celestial Dragon. He reminded himself of his goal once again.
‘In selecting the location of dispatch for the Celestial Dragon’s Gate Search Team, the Guild Master’s will take over about for 90% of the decision.’
The primary goal was to find out the critical factor affecting the decision. The intruder hid in the Guild Master’s office along the pre-identified route. Seo Jin-Wook inherited the place where Seo Gyu-Cheol originally used.
‘[Penetration!]’ He scanned the inside once again.
‘As expected, there’s a separate server only for the Guild Master.’
The secret of the Guild Master that wasn’t shared with other guild members should have been here. When a man plugged a microchip into a server, the hacking tool was activated. While the chip broke down the server’s security network and copied data without a trace, he noticed that it was his second target.
‘Safe!’ The man approached the wall of the office without hesitation. On the surface, it looked like an ordinary structure, visible to him. A barrier firmly protected the huge safe.
Chak! Cha-chak! Even though he had prepared in advance, the man had difficulty opening the safe. As if to imply how precious the item it protected was, the lock was like solid iron. After dismantling all the artifacts used to magic, the tightly closed door eventually opened.
The man’s eyes widened, ‘It’s the Guild Master’s sword!’
Finding clues to unlock the secret of Seo Jin-Wook’s remarkably fast growth rate
was one of the requests, and some people suspected that growth beyond the realm of pure talent was due to special items. Seo Jin-Wook’s most representative item known to the public was…
‘The sword that only himself knows about its details.’
There was no alarm magic or barrier on the sword itself.
‘First, let’s analyze its value.’
After finding out what it was, he planned to steal it and run away if everything went south. The man opened a [Analysis] scroll with one hand and carefully stretched out the other towards the sword. The moment he grabbed the handle of the sword, he heard someone whispering in his head.
‘······Sigh, you stupid bastard.’
The intruder stiffened his body, and then his eyes became blurred.

chapters.title: Chapter 86
chapters.content:
[Thanks for the continued support on NU! This series is very hard to translate and most chapters are 50% longer than usual KR web novels (with some chapters reaching 3800 words). Please consider supporting us by reading ahead. Each 36 cents USD and would go a long way in supporting both the quality and quantity of our uploads. Right off my head, I believe that this series is still in the red in the four digits!]
Moths (2)
I opened the door and entered. The intruder had turned stiff like a stone still holding the sword. I concentrated Mana on my hand as I looked at that sight.
“Did it work?”
If the answer didn’t come back immediately, I was about to rush in and hold him down. However, the intruder’s lips moved and said the sentence I wanted, “It worked, the whispers.”
The man’s pupils shook and gradually stabilized, which was evidence of successful brainwashing. It was not the intruder but the sword that answered through the body, as it was instructed to transfer its words instead of his own.
“That’s a relief.”
The devil’s sword’s brainwashing skill [Whisper of the Sword] had a success rate ranked A, which was statistically around 50%. As soon as the intruder grabbed the handle of the devil’s sword, it planned to use the skill, and each countermeasure was arranged depending on whether it worked or not. Fortunately, the brainwashing worked, so things were likely to be easy from now on.
“Please order him to follow my instructions and answer my questions from now on.”
First, the intruder simply released Polymorph when instructed to identify himself. When I saw him in his original face, I recognized who he was. His lips moved.
“My name is Dideric van Dyke.”
I clicked my tongue, “They invited a big man, didn’t they?”
The identity of the intruder was a Dutch SS-Rank hunter who was also famous in my previous life. Because of his peculiar skill tree, he gained his notoriety by dealing with work in the shadows such as intelligence and assassination rather than exploring the dungeons.
‘When I first heard the name, he was mostly commissioned by governments, but I guess it was still before he got to that level.’
He is the No. 1 Hunter in the industry, who had no rival in that field of work in his previous life. The reason why he disappeared suddenly in his last life was…
‘He broke in to kidnap Angelica at the request of the Chinese government, and he was caught by the barriers that Hibiki laid out.’
Angelica, unperturbed, struck the captured Dideric’s neck, but that was buried as a secret that only 5 of the Guild Masters knew.
‘However, the collapse of the country called China took place less than a year after the incident.’
It would be no coincidence if I thought that the frequency of predictions about the Chinese dungeons had decreased since the kidnapping attempt.
‘Anyway, now I know his identity.’
He was going to be a lot bigger in the future, but at this point, Dideric was not a hunter who could be moved with little money.
“What about the client?”
He answered, “Grand Croix Guild.”
“Hah,” It was so lame that I was about to laugh.
‘I was leaving them alone only because they were pushed out of the top.’
The fact that he was actively digging up his grave to lie down and even carving his coffin left me no choice but to live up to his expectations.
“What about the content of the request?”
Dideric easily answered, “First, hack data from the dedicated server that only the Guild Master Seo Jin-Wook can access. Second, uncover the secrets of rapid growth, such as the items he uses. Third…”
My eyebrows wiggled when I heard the last request.
“… When secured and if conditions allow after observation, assassinate the Guild Master Seo Jin-Wook.”
There he crossed the line again. I sighed shallow and scratched my head.
“He must have been very nervous as well, Kim Kyung-Rok.”
Next, I asked how this request was related to the Grand Croix Guild. Of course, they wouldn’t have told Dideric such information. Still, I asked because I assumed that Dideric, who was able to be commissioned, had secretly identified the client. Sure enough, he named several more executives besides the Guild Master Kim Kyung-Rok.
“Then…” My next words were not for Dideric but for the devil’s sword, “I’m going to have to ask you to do a job for me.”
I didn’t even come into contact with the sword, but I had the sense from the sigh it was leaking telepathically and somehow flowing into my mind.
*
A few hours later, Kim Kyung-Rok asked, “What time is it now?”
“It’s almost 6 a.m.,” came back the reply.
It was still early to go to work, but Kim Kyung-Rok and three high-ranking hunters gathered together in the Grand Croix meeting room.
Kim Kyung-Rok grumbled, “I mean, why is that bastard taking so long without at least updating us that the job was successful or not?”
“Exactly. He said he was going to start infiltrating around 2 a.m. and was going to take about a couple of hours at most.”
“That’s why are we sitting here up all night!”
Kim Kyung-Rok, who had spent a lot of money hiring Dideric, could not sleep and, therefore, was waiting for the results in the conference room, staying up all night with three other guild members who were in on the plan.
And then. Creek. Suddenly, the conference room door opened. Kim Kyung-Rok thought that perhaps the secretary had come to work early for some reason.
‘She’s only diligent on days like this when I didn’t order her to do so.’
He shouted in an irritated tone, “Hey! We’re in a meeting right now, so don’t come in until I call you!”
There was no response. As the door completely opened, the four hunters’ eyes in the conference room all turned toward it.
“What is it?”
There was nobody outside the open door. Creek. Naturally, the door closed again. Only then did the seated four hunters stand up in unison. But it’s already too late.
Phuk!
The blade popped out through the neck of a giant hunter sitting closest to the meeting room door.
“Gak!”
In that state, the air shook, and a man revealed himself. He took out a scroll with his unarmed hand and tore it. At the same time, powerful energy spread through the conference room.
“It’s a barrier!”
Now, no one could go out or come in for some time. Everything happened in a flash. Kim Kyung-Rok’s eyes grew bigger when he noticed the identity of the opponent, “You!”
He had never met him face to face because he made a deal through an agent, but there was no way he couldn’t recognize his face. The opponent was Dideric van Dyke, who he had entrusted with the task. Kim Kyung-Rok was shocked.
‘That crazy bastard!’
He took out the weapon he always carried with him and aimed at his opponent.
‘Why, all of a sudden? Was he persuaded to do otherwise?’ Heat rose in his head, and his thought process sped up. Meanwhile, Dideric pulled out the sword with a blank expression.
Phuk!
The neck was pierced, but A-Rank Hunter did not die immediately.
“Ghhhh!”
The red foam flowed down along his neckline with a bubbling sound. Dideric swung his arm as he looked at it.
Swish!
The severed head shot up into the sky and fell on the conference room floor, and rolled. Their eyes widened again.
Phuk!
Diderick thrust a knife into the chest of Hunter’s body, which was laid on the floor. Then…Gulp, gulp. Shoo!
“Well, well, what the hell is that?”
The blade that dug into the body began to gobble up the remaining blood from the body. It attacked the large one first because he was closest, but the being that manipulated Dideric van Dyke thought with a mental smile, ‘First of all, if it has a large capacity, there will be a lot to eat.’
In the blink of an eye, the body turned into a mummy with only the skin left. After absorbing the human species’ blood, the devil’s sword moved Dideric to take care of the remains for the first time in such a long time.
Boosh!
The sword energy burning on the blade completely burned a dead body, like a wooden shell, into ash. It was because of Seo Jin-Wook’s request not to leave any more traces than necessary.
‘Anyway, he’s such a bother!’
While he was grumbling inside, “Strike him!”
The remaining three hunters rushed in at once. When it saw them, it mentally sighed.
‘Those morons.’
Perhaps because they were in the tutorial’s early days, there was something awkward to the Awakened of this world.
The devil’s sword, who controlled the Dideric with the [Whisper of the Sword], thought to himself, ‘It took three seconds for them to react to a colleague being struck.’
If Seo Jin-Wook himself had come, he would have slaughtered all of them even before they could respond.
Shing! A great amount of sword pressure swept in front, along the path where Dideric sliced with large arcs.
“K-argh!” After blocking the two far away, its eyes met with a man close by. Dideric’s left hand quickly picked up the giant ax that the giant held.
“Die!” Dideric stopped the long sword from flying with the ax and struck Hunter’s thigh with a sword.
Hunter screamed and knelt, “Aaargh!”
It was a scene that made him snicker as he watched it, ‘They can’t even bear this much pain, and they’re unable to fight in an instant? Anyway, humans.’
They were comparable to some belligerent species that crawled with their arms left when their legs are torn apart, and even when their arms were torn off, they bit with their teeth.
‘But the only advantage is that their blood doesn’t taste bad.’
Outside the dungeon, there were so many things all over the place to eat like this. The devil’s sword clicked his tongue, lamenting its situation. Seo Jin-Wook usually only fed it the blood of the beasts. Therefore, today was the day to relieve its frustration after a long time. But then, the devil’s sword cut the kneeling one’s throat and saw the hunters rushing in from behind. It was a quick move, but the devil’s sword was looking into their gap.
‘The clumsiest sword movement ever.’ The blade of the sword moved without even leaving any afterimage. The sound of tearing in the air rang twice. Chaaak! Hunter’s body was cut into dozens of pieces. The conference room was full of blood, but that was also only for a while.
Swoosh!
When the blade of the sword touched the floor, it sucked up all of the blood that had been spraying while it ebbed.
‘It’s a meal after a long time; I shouldn’t leave anything behind.’
Kim Kyung-Rok, who alone survived, and had a pale face, muttered, “You punk!” His head was a mess.
‘He’s an SS-Rank hunter, but he said his specialty was stealth and assassination.’
As long as he deliberately revealed himself, he thought he had a good chance of winning. That one S-Rank Hunter and three A-Rank Hunters…. would be able to deal with at least one SS-Rank Hunter. Besides, the information obtained suggested that Dideric’s skill tree was vulnerable to a face-to-face battle, so once he fails to ambush, he would run away without hesitation. But then, ‘ What the hell was that sword movement?’ Kim Kyung-Rok’s eyes couldn’t even catch up with him properly.
Boosh! The two bodies, which had their blood drained in an instant, were also completely burned down. Dry glances shifted toward the stiffened-up Kim Kyung-Rok. The devil’s sword’s low whisper echoed through the vocal cords of the SS-Ranked Hunter with a chilling voice.
“Will you try to resist?”
“This….!” Kim Kyung-Rok activated his unique skill.
[Super Regeneration!]
The devil’s sword that could not see Mana except for the one applied on its physical self, the sword, but it noticed that he did something, and as a result, the atmosphere changed.
“I don’t know what that is.” The blade of the devil’s sword, aimed by Diderick, was directed at the opponent, “Since I can’t eat your blood anyway.”
After an incomprehensible remark, “It’s been a while since I’ve done this; make me have some fun. I had a lot that I kept suppressed.”
“Crazy bastard, die!” Kim Kyung-Rok charged with his sword. He concentrated Mana on one point with all his might and pushed it in, along the trajectory towards the neck of Dideric. Suddenly, a harsh light in Kim Kyung-Rok’s eyes shone.
‘It’s working!’
When having swung the sword for a long time, you develop a sense. If you swing the sword along the sword path in your head, you will know where the irreversible point is. The moment the sword reaches that point, the victory or defeat is already decided.
Kim Kyung-Rok realized that his sword had just passed that point. That even if the sky and the ground turn upside down, or the universe collapsed, the sword would cut the opponent’s breath. Right before that moment was about to be successful…Clang! A sharp sound of friction was heard, and the low, heavy echo of metal. Kim Kyung-Rok felt his bones ringing. A shiver was felt down his spine. He saw Dideric’s snake-like eyes that had just approached, right in front of him.
“How!”
The sword, held tight enough to turn his hands pale, shook. His gaze was fixed on the point where the blades crossed each other. Kim Kyung-Rok’s sword, which was on an unstoppable track, was blocked by Dideric.
‘What was that?!’
At the point at which the devil’s sword began to move, and the point at which it reached, only those two points existed, but there was no line connecting the points. At least in Kim Kyung-Rok’s eyes, it was invisible.
‘It was a mistake!’
Only now did he realize that there were also swords that moved outside the world that he perceived—a groan leaked between his clenched teeth.
“K-hpppp!”
The blade of the devil’s sword rained down, drawing curved lines. Dideric’s sword path was fierce and sharp. Storm-like energy stretched along the ends of his swing. The burning sword energy changed its character respective to the change of waves. While the exchange of attack with the sword took place a few times, Kim Kyung-Rok noticed another thing.
‘How much sword mastery is he using?!’
He had the eyes to distinguish swordsmanship mastery. Characteristics that were hidden in the movement beyond the color and shape difference of sword energy. Every time Dideric’s sword swung, it exploded with subtle changes.
And in the end, puhk!
The moment when the devil’s sword cut Kim Kyung-Rok’s shoulder and dug into it, he managed to pull himself back by the force of desperation. Then one of Dideric’s eyebrows went up.
“Hmm?”
Shhhh!
Kim Kyung-Rok’s wound, which had been cut in half, was seen coming together again.
The devil’s sword understood the situation, “It’s a regenerative type of skill.”
And, as far as the devil’s sword knew, “That type of skill has a time limit,” he giggled and talked, “Well, I can cut and cut as much as I want for a few minutes without worrying about killing him.”
Drip. Cold sweat flowed down Kim Kyung-Rok’s back when he heard those words.
The devil’s sword muttered as he lifted Dideric’s arm.
“Please hang in there for a long time. For me.”
*
Exactly 5 minutes later, the devil’s sword watched Kim Kyung-Rok sitting on the floor, shaking. In that short time, Kim Kyung-Rok’s expression had completely changed. His face was covered with tears and mucus, trembling like a little child.
He said, crawling on the floor, “P-Ple…. Plea….”
Dideric said in a casual tone, “What? Is your skill already done?”
He thrust the sword into Kim Kyung-Rok’s elbow joint, but no generation took place this time. It was not clear whether he intentionally stopped his unique skill or whether the allotted time was over. The devil’s sword thought of letting Kim Kyung-Rok’s body answer, to be sure, but soon lost his interest and decided to quit.
“Well, shall we stop here?”
Kim Kyung-Rok nodded several times as he trembled. It was so intense, to the point that it was worrisome that his neck bone would break. The short few minutes of skill activation felt like years in Kim Kyung-Rok’s head. He could not even remember how many pieces his body had been cut and reattached due to the devil’s sword and how many times he had been stabbed, cut, and healed. He just wanted to get out of this hellish situation quickly.
Meanwhile, ‘Man, this isn’t fun at all, is it?’
It was not only Kim Kyung-Rok’s reaction that broke the devil’s sword’s enthusiasm. The Mana of the temporary host, Dideric, who was moving by the [Whisper of the Sword], also played a part. You could feel a series of processes that absorb Mana from the core of the person holding him and amplify it with a blade. However, after a long time of having the Mana of a human being other than Seo Jin-Wook on the blade, it felt a distinguishable change.
‘Damn it, that bastard just left my taste buds to shit.’
It wasn’t just that. The body of the Awakened overcame limitations and became stronger with Mana’s activation. Dideric was also an SS-Rank hunter, and despite the devil’s sword directing his movement, it felt completely different from when Seo Jin-Wook swung. All factors, such as nervous system reactions, explosive power depending on muscle strength, and skeleton flexibility, were not satisfactory. The devil’s sword clicked his tongue inwardly.
‘It’s not going to be fun even if I were to continue.’
Dideric was supposed to use it once and be thrown away anyway. It was because Dideric always had to hold the sword in his hand to maintain the [Whisper of the Sword], but there was no way that Seo Jin-Wook would allow it.
‘The playtime is over.’
Dideric’s body moved, and the blade came into contact with Kim Kyung-Rok’s body.
With the other arm, it led the sword that Kim Kyung-Rok held and aimed at the heart of Dideric. And he placed his own weight on the blade.
Puhk!
Riiiip!
Setting up the scene of mutual killing was simple, as long as the opponent completely lost his will. Just like that, the devil’s sword penetrated Kim Kyung-Rok’s neck, and Kim Kyung-Rok’s sword pierced Dideric’s heart, and the light of Mana completely disappeared from the two cores.
Swish!
Diderick’s shadow shook, and a figure popped out, “······Uhhhhhhh!”
It was a zombie. The zombie holding the ordinary sword in Dideric’s hand retrieved the devil’s sword and held it.
‘Damn it, I was prepared, but I’m offended! To let the half-decayed corpse grab on me!’
The devil’s sword’s telepathy resonated, but the zombie did not respond. Silently, following Nate’s directions from afar, it tore the scroll once again. As soon as that happened…
Paht!
Teleportation was triggered, and a flash covered the zombies and the devil’s sword, and they disappeared. All that was left in the Grand Croix’s conference room was Dideric and Kim Kyung-Rok’s bodies, who had killed and ripped each other.

chapters.title: Chapter 87
chapters.content:
Screening Quest (1)
The discovery of the Grand Croix Guild’s head as a cold corpse in the conference room shook the whole country. There were many suspicious things about the incident. It was a scene where it was believed that he died by battling with a Dutch SS-Ranked hunter, working as a freelancer, who ended up mutually killing each other. But why the two had fought for their lives in the conference room in the first place was unknown. This was because the media had no idea about the true nature of the private business run by Dideric Van Dyke.
Furthermore, three of Grand Croix’s ace Hunters were also missing. There were signs of them entering the building on the same day, but there was no sign of them leaving. Police and the Hunter Management were trying to locate the missing persons, convinced they were also involved in the incident.
‘Go ahead and search, as if you’ll find any evidence,’ I thought while turning off the news, ‘By the way, it’s natural for it to follow orders according to the contract… but the work was done pretty neat.’
Even though I allowed it to go on a night out for the first time, the devil’s sword’s reaction when it returned was mediocre. I found it strange because it was dissatisfied even though it tasted blood for the first time in a long time. However, the reaction might be, I thought, was that it did its job properly anyway.
‘I’ll have to utilize it from time to time. With Nate’s accompanying subordinate, it’s easy to retrieve as well.’
While I thought so, bee-bee-bee-beep, there was a ring.
“Huh?”
It was the Senator. As I gestured, a hologram popped up.
“You keep in touch with me a lot these days.”
Looking at the time, it was the middle of the night in America. Was it something urgent? The Senator in the hologram said with a stiff look. “A lot of things come up that I have to talk to you in person.”
“Looking at the time, I don’t think it’s good news.”
There was still time left until the mass-production of artifacts produced by the joint venture was released to the media. There wouldn’t be an issue if they just wrapped it up with the last feedback I sent.
“Is this about the Artifact?”
He shook his head, “No, it’s something else. I was wondering if you had any information about it. I’d like to ask you for advice. Although I don’t know how much you can find out with that ‘power.’”
The Senator didn’t know, until to the point, that I have a unique skill called [The Successor’s Eyes], but he was sure that I have intelligence type abilities.
He frowned a little and said, “There seems to be a problem in China.”
Oh, is it finally starting? It was about time for the information to leak out. Hearing that opened my ears because the problem he mentioned may have been the historical event I was waiting for.
“What’s the situation?”
“Look.” He floated a map next to the hologram. The area pointed by the arrow was a suburb about 30 kilometers from downtown Beijing.
‘It’s right!’ Anyway, I pretended not to know, whatever his state might be, “Is it a satellite city near Beijing?”
“This city is also part of Beijing by its administrative district. Anyway, there seemed to be an accident at the gate here.”
“You keep speaking in a tone suggesting it’s all but speculations.”
“Yeah, even the U.S. government hasn’t got the exact information on what’s going on here either. Look at this.”
Another thing that floated next to it was a satellite photo. A thick layer of cloud could be seen concentrated in the area.
“Winter in Beijing is cold and dry. The chance of snowy rain in this season is close to zero. But then, the area within 5km radius of the gate has already been experiencing a month of locally heavy rain.”
In terms of style, it was not done by aliens. I say as if I had guessed it, “The Chinese government must have induced artificial rainfall in the region. The reason why they kept it there for a month is. To avoid satellite imagery of what’s happening there?”
“Yes, you understand it well,” The Senator’s expression became more serious, “I don’t know what they’re doing, but it’s not like a secret experiment. People’s Army tank units and Awakened troops continue to gather nearby, and it seems to be the purpose of surrounding the area.”
Unless the government can pour artificial rain all across China, the troop movements that started in other regions will inevitably be exposed.
“The U.S. is also testing the water of China through various diplomatic channels, but they aren’t giving a single clue while keeping their mouth shut. So, the high-ranking officials at the State Department are sleepless. According to history so far, the more China comes out like that, it reveals later that the bigger the accident is. After it’s too late.”
I nodded. It was an accurate guess.
‘I didn’t know exactly when that gate Clear was successful. In the past life, the Chinese government didn’t release any information, and after the government collapsed, the data disappeared altogether.’
Assuming that things in the past life have continued as they were this time, shortly after they Cleared the problematic gate dungeon, the dungeon boundary would have collapsed. And as the Ersmann and the immortal did before, other-dimensional species came to Earth.
‘The Chinese government failed to put down the initial fire and completely lost control of a few kilometers of the gate radius. Since then, they kept the fact strictly confidential.’
The Communist Party desperately tried to prevent the fact that aliens occupied mainland China from being known to the citizens or other countries.
‘They thought that they’d lose face.’
The Senator said, “Considering the characteristics of the government, it is clear that they are trying to deal with it on their own without informing the outside world. But it’s taking too long. If it has not been resolved for a month, it will likely continue to be so. And the concern from our side is··.”
“They’re concerned about the problems that China has not solved, causing the other countries to be affected as well.”
“Exactly. If it’s a problem caused by the gate, it’s either of the two: It could be a dungeon break or an alien invasion. Either way, if they don’t handle it in the beginning, it’ll be a big headache.”
That’s exactly what happened in my previous life, “First of all, although I don’t have any information in my hands right now,” I lied, “I’ll find more about it.”
I avoided further details on how I will find out about it.
“Oh, and don’t think about going to China yourself,” The Senator threatened, “You know how things go around there, don’t you? There are more than one or two hunters who went missing after stepping on Chinese soil. You can’t be relaxed because you’re an SS-Rank hunter.”
“Oh, I know too well.” China forcibly conscripted all Awakened in their country and ran a unit of them. It was famous that even foreign Awakened who enter the country often disappear without a trace.
“And besides, you’re not American! They wouldn’t even hesitate to do so!”
“Don’t worry about that.”
I mumbled after I ended the call with the Senator, “There will be no official visit.”
*
