Using [Multiple Cognition] that was almost always active from the moment she woke up until she went to bed, she assembled and disassembled Mana in various patterns in her body.
It was a training method that repeated the process until right before magic was invoked.
“Meow!”
At her feet, sitting on a chair and concentrating, an animal resembling a tuxedo cat approached her and rubbed its soft fur against her legs. It then gently wrapped her ankle with its long tail.
“Are you done eating?”
At the same time she drew the Mana signature of 3 kinds of spells, Hibiki extended her hand below and caressed the head of Iponia.
“Cat, do you want me to play with you?”
Iponia jumped onto the desk as if it felt her reaction was rather passive. It laid down with its stomach exposed and stared at Hibiki’s face. It was a blatant demonstration.
Despite Seo Jin-Wook’s effort to raise it ever since it was a baby, the first person it completely lowered its guard to was Hibiki.
Instead of Seo Jin-Wook, who often left the house, Hibiki took full care of it lately.
It was also her job to feed the card to it and manage the crystals it spat out.
“I don’t think you’re ever tired of it.”
As the Mana pattern for the S-Rank [Fire Buster] spell was shaped and dissipated when it was about to be invoked, Hibiki shook the green foxtail-shaped toy with one hand.
Iponia stretched its front paws into the air as if to scratch it. It soon began to concentrate on playing.
‘He said we had to raise it since there was a job waiting for it and that he didn’t bring it here just to keep it as a pet.’
That time, while practicing the pattern of electric spells, she recalled what Seo Jin-Wook said.
‘Can it be that he’ll feed a card of a great rank that it cannot digest yet… To get its crystal?’
While Hibiki was curious in that manner…
“…!”
She sensed something which caused her expression to stiffen.
Other than training to form several spells in unison and playing with a dungeon creature named Cat even though it wasn’t a cat– at that time, Hibiki was also doing another job.
That was because Seo Jin-Wook had also handed over control installed around the house.
With her senses connected to them, she monitored her surroundings as if she were watching the security cameras, and there were signs of abnormality.
“They’re here!”
Nate knocked on the door as if he had been waiting when she urgently contacted him through her terminal.
When she opened the door, he had already changed into a combat uniform and was smiling with a calm face.
“You ready?”
He noded.
“Meooow.”
Iponia cried as if to protest when she suddenly stopped playing with it.
Hibiki floated it in the air with her psychokinesis.
Seeing that, Nate stretched a shadow without saying a word.
Iponia must have felt ominous since it tried to run away with its four feet struggling in the air.
“Meoooooow!”
“I’m sorry, Cat. Stay inside for a while.”
Hibiki, who tucked Iponia into Nate’s shadow, turned her head again and made eye contact with him.
She was also waiting for that moment, having changed into the combat uniform.
“Did you get the scroll?”
“Of course!”
He took out the SSS-Rank [Wide-Rage Teleport] scroll given by Seo Jin-Wook and showed it to her. It was an item that had never been distributed to the Earthlings of that era.
With only a little Mana injected, it ripped away and teleported the two to their designated location.
For the Matap Guild, there was no way to de-spell SSS-Class magic, so it was like a lifeline in case of emergency.
‘Can we do it properly?’
The two knew who they were going to face that day.
However, that was their first time to fight against the Awakened.
Seo Jin-Wook gave them advice while informing them of the plan.
‘You can just use the scroll and run away in any case, but I think they’re at a level that’s low enough for you two to deal with.’
It didn’t make sense, the fact that two S-Class hunters could handle four SS-Class hunters.
However, Seo Jin-Wook pointed out that Nate and Hibiki weren’t any ordinary S-Class Awakened and that their equipped items were also of a different level.
‘I’ll finish my part as soon as I can and catch up, so don’t worry too much.’
Recalling Seo Jin-Wook’s reassuring words, Hibiki once again strengthened her will.
‘I can’t let him down.’
The two quickly moved out of their home.
It was a scheduled escape that began in due course so that the opponent could chase them with tracking magic.
*
Sometime after the two of them left, a series of intruders hid inside the house.
Arthur Clifford planned to kidnap even a close aide who might know his secrets if Seo Jin-Wook didn’t talk or resistance was unbreakable.
It was natural that Nate and Hibiki were chosen as targets.
They were skilled people who blocked the A-Class break together, and they were close enough to live in the house altogether.
“Tsk, they’ve already noticed and ran.”
Looking at the empty room, the Matap’s hunter clicked his tongue.
The men in charge of the house were two swordsmen and two wizards.
The target they were aiming for had already disappeared.
“Is it possible to track them?”
“Wait for a moment.”
A wizard recited a spell.
[Trail Seeker!]
He looked around with blue light lingering in his eyes.
“That’s a relief. It hasn’t been long since they left. They’re traceable.”
The wizard moved, staring at the traces of movement that were only visible to his eyes.
“This way.”
*
The two quickly got out of their home on the back of a zombie with a Haste spell.
They sprinted with the wind on the ridge where the darkness took place.
It was also due to Seo Jin-Wook’s instructions, who considered that civilians would be caught in the firefight if they started the battle in the residential area, but Nate would’ve done that even if he didn’t ask him to.
‘If we break Jin-Wook’s house one more time, we might be kicked out of his house for real this time!’
It was a serious concern for him.
“… I think we’re far enough from the city now. They followed right behind us!”
Hibiki, who was calculating the distance from the opponent with observation-type magic, gave a signal.
The Orcs, which were running while carrying them behind, stopped.
As they waited for a moment, the pursuers appeared.
“Haha! You must’ve given up now. That’s a wise choice.”
The Awakened of the Matap Guild quickly formed a siege.
At the same time, two swordsmen pulled out their swords and blocked the front.
Weing!
The two wizards that rose into the air with the [Levitation] spell flew slightly apart and blocked their escape routes.
They left an adequate distance that also served as a vantage point. Even if Nate and Hibiki escaped, they could track them right away, and they could bombard them with various spells as well.
‘The frontline on the ground are the close-ranged fighters, and the rear is composed of wizards in the air.’
Hibiki simulated a plan in her head.
In the meantime, the swordsman urged their surrender in a calm voice.
“Seo Jin-Wook is not in Seoul right now.”
“…”
“Do you understand? It means no one would be able to help. You two can’t beat us.”
He giggled and revealed his teeth.
“For the sake of both of us, don’t be troublesome and waste energy. Just follow me. If you don’t bother us, we’ll take you both with your arms and legs still attached.”
“…”
Nate and Hibiki simply stared quietly at them and didn’t reply.
The swordsman assumed that the attitude was because they were tensed up from nervousness and fear.
‘It’s rumored that those two received an S-Rank because they were lucky. In the end, they are still rookies. It’s been less than a year since they Awakened, after all. If I scare them moderately, it will be enough to convince them.’
But that prediction was wrong.
Swoosh!
As if to cover the two, numerous monster-type zombies were summoned.
“Rarrgh…!”
“Grrrrr…!”
The disgusting smell pierced the noses of the Awakened mixed in the night breeze.
The swordsman frowned because of displeasure and irritation.
The Rune Stone began to glow as the wizards in the air quietly prepared for captivity spells.
“You’re bothering me.”
He ground his teeth and threatened them.
“They say what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger. You both wouldn’t die of shock even if I cut one of your arms off. Consider the hope of being dragged away in one piece as gone!”
Nate and Hibiki stood their ground as they waited for the right time while their enemies approached.
They didn’t need to wait long either.
Weing!
At that moment, the swords held by the two swordsmen were coated with sword energy.
– Threats to the security target found!
Telepathy rang in his head.
Simultaneously, the expression of the being that only Nate could see on that spot quickly changed.
It was a being shaped like a woman, composed of blue Mana.
The Spirit, who had only observed the situation expressionlessly despite the very urgent situations, now glared at the Matap swordsmen with a hostile look.
Shhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!
Light flashed above the heads of the two.
As the flash disappeared, what was summoned was a magnificent metal structure floating in the air.
“Huh?”
What came to mind of the Matap guild members after seeing it was the large-calibered multi-round cannon.
It was an item that they saw for the first time, but it was not difficult to imagine how it would work.
Instead of panicking, they shifted to defense formation immediately.
[Conditional Barrier (Rank: S)]
[Aerial Shield (Rank: A)]
The two wizards each performed their own defensive magic.
A golden cloud cover enveloped one person’s body.
In front of the other, the atmosphere swirled, and a cohesive shield was formed.
Whooooooo!
The two swordsmen on the ground also prepared for an attack by concentrating Mana throughout their bodies.
That was because hundreds of caliber openings aimed at them were likely to shoot fire and pour bullets at any moment.
But then…
“… ?!”
– Warning! Warning! No further access is allowed. It will respond with immediate firing in case of non-response…
They clicked their tongue inside.
‘What a fool!’
Instead of attacking right away after summoning an item like that, he’s only threatening them.
‘That’s why they’re called rookies!’
Thanks to that, they were already perfectly in defense positions themselves.
It would be bearable even if it poured out attacks like that since it’s a shield formed by the Mana output of an SS-Rank hunter.
‘We must take him down first!’
Tat!
He kicked the ground, swallowing a laugh of ridicule inside.
When the sword’s trajectory was heading beyond the undead to Nate–
“… ?!”
Hibiki activated a spell targeting the air.
The target was not the swordsman who rushed immediately.
It was the wizards in the air, hidden behind defensive magic.
[De-spell!]
Right after that, the two wizards became baffled by the sudden change of scenery.
“… Huh?”
It didn’t take long for them to notice that they were falling.
Beyond the overturned vision, they wondered.
‘How?’
They couldn’t understand.
[De-spell] wasn’t a ranged attack. Once triggered, there was only one spell that could be voided.
What they noticed while they were crashing, amid the scenery that was flowing like water, was the fact that the two wizards were falling at the same time, and the shield that protected them also disappeared.
That was two floating magic and two protective magic spells.
Four kinds of spells were nulled instantly.
That phenomenon was impossible unless someone recited and activated four de-spell spells at the same time.
At that moment, a strange concept passed through the minds of wizards.
‘Multiple… recitation?’
They tried to recite the spell as a reflex, but their attempt was stopped as soon as telepathy penetrated their heads sharply.
– Fire!
As they were placed in a state where they were helplessly exposed to a beast, the two magicians fell.
Right about the moment when the swordsmen that wrapped their entire bodies with Mana Barrier rushed in–
Shhhh!
The zombies surrounding Nate and Hibiki disappeared instantly.
At the same time, when nothing but the air occupied the space, light exploded.
Pa-pa-pat!
Boo-boo-boo-boom!
The large-calibered multi-round cannon was aimed in both directions and started to fire.
The number of light bullets it shot in a second reached thousands of rounds.
The energy shells that struck their naked bodies literally ripped through and stirred up the wizards. The two crash-landers quickly disappeared amid a blizzard of light that poured in a straight line.
Boo-boo-boo-boom!
The swordsmen who were fully armed with the Mana armor, unaffected by the [De-spell], were better off.
However, it never meant that it was easy for them.
“Keeeup!”
The magic bullets that crashed on the thick shield shook his bones and crushed his muscles.
The trajectory of the attack towards Nate stopped. They simply couldn’t move any further in the face of the bullet barrier.
They, who experienced the might of an item beyond common sense with their bodies, were horrified that their souls would escape their bodies.
‘What… kind of ridiculous thing is that?! From where did they find that kind of weapon?!’
The freedom to hold such thoughts in their heads soon disappeared as well.
“K-Aaargh!”
In the middle of the storm of unforgiving bullets, each bullet struck them down with heavy shock.
The shooting continued until the item used up the fully charged Mana.
And finally…
“…”
Light bullets stopped firing.
At that moment, the telepathy rang in Nate’s head.
– Warning! Warning! The Mana charged in this security system has been exhausted.
– Confirming the survival of the threat target. Emergency! Emergency!
– Asking for aid from other nearby beings through the collective intelligence network… No connection. Access denied!
– Continuous protection by this security system is not available at this time. The protected subject must immediately escape to a safe place and request protection from the Imperial Government!
The face of the Spirit, which was mostly expressionless and hostile, had become pale.
Its expression was as if the fire had fallen on its foot.
It was always like that when the charged Mana was depleted.
Nate calmly replied because he didn’t experience it only once or twice.
“… It’s okay. I’ll take care of the rest.”
– It’s dangerous! Retreat!
The Spirit formed by blue light gradually turned blurry. It disappeared as if it was sucked into Nate’s neck. It required sufficient time to recharge once activated.
The Spirit continued to send anxious telepathy to Nate even as it disappeared.
– … Danger!
– I must… protect… you…!
Paht!
After the Spirit completely disappeared into the neck tattoo, Nate looked at the tragedy that unfolded in front of him.
Hibiki, who was reeling from Mana exhaustion, managed to get herself together by chugging a potion down.
“… Indeed, it’s incredible.”
The direction of the wizard, in which bullets were poured into the sky, was rather decent. The two, who received the attack with their bare bodies, were evaporated to blood fog before their bodies fell to the ground, leaving no trace.
A devastated landscape unfolded along the poured bullets’ trajectory in the direction that aimed for the targets on the ground.
Nate, who partially created a barren hill, noded, saying that it was a good thing he was as far away from home as possible.
“… Keee-!”
The two swordsmen, who were all battered up, were staring at them amid the smoke.
It was clear that they had spent a considerable amount of Mana to stop the bullet storm.
“You bastards!”
Instead of continuing to stare at them, Nate looked up.
At the same time–
Swoosh!
A strong wind, incomparable to that which took place while summoning the Orc zombies a while ago, blew.
“···?!”
The two swordsmen moved their eyes after Nate’s gaze while filled with overwhelming anxiety.
In the direction they stared, there it was.
Deeper darkness covered the night sky in a pointed form.
It was a humongous floating body.
Krrrrrrrrr!
In the strange sense of twisted law of perspective, two survivors recalled their memories.
The reason why four SS-Class members had to be mobilized to catch two S-Class members in the first place was because of the contingency they wanted to be prepared for.
“… Dragon!”
Seo Jin-Wook was not the one who could control the dragon.
The two people belatedly realized that it was not a living dragon but an undead dragon.
But as mentioned, they were too late.
Crrrrrrrrr!
Its yellow eyes looked down on them.
The giant creature’s mouth opened, reflecting a red flame blazing inside its sharp teeth on the swordsmen’s retina.
Kwhaaaaaa!
A river of flame connected the sky and the ground.
That was the last scene that the two swordsmen saw before they died.
*
“Oh, really? That’s great. I don’t have to go that far, then. Well done.”
I felt relieved as I ended the call with Hibiki.
The two seemed to have dealt with the invaders without any problems.
‘Yes, considering their abilities and items, the odds were good.’
It was an expected result.
I turned my eyes to the body of an S-Class hunter rolling on the floor.
‘Both of them are only called S-Rank, but they’re different from this guy.’
He was sprawled next to the bluely lit Gate, a hole visible on his chest.
Boosh!
After burning him completely without a trace, I headed to the next destination.
‘They must anxiously be waiting for the results right now, aren’t they?’
That day’s second destination was the Destructional Blade guild.

chapters.title: Chapter 103
chapters.content:
[Premium Completed!]
Destruction Blade
Early in the morning, when office workers make their ways to work, a foreigner entered the Destruction Blade building located in the middle of Gangnam.
Wearing watches, a suit, and shoes that anyone would know were expensive at a glance, the man walked across the lobby on the first floor with a subtle smile worn on his lips.
All eyes were on him.
“Huh? That foreigner… Doesn’t he seem familiar?”
It didn’t take long for them to recognize the celebrity in the same field of work.
One person’s name started to be mentioned around by the people’s mouths.
“Pshh, no way. It can’t be. Westerners all look alike to each other.”
“No, I’m sure! I saw it on the news. He looks exactly like him!”
Leaving the murmur behind him, the foreigner who headed straight to the information desk began to speak.
He had a gentle British accent.
“I have an appointment with Guild Master Seo Moon-Ga-In.”
“Yes, pardon me, but what is your name?”
The foreigner replied warmly.
“Arthur Clifford.”
*
Seo Moon-Ga-In sat behind her desk with a shadow cast on her face.
She stayed up all night waiting for news.
Doubts were in her mind.
‘What the hell is going on?’
Arthur Clifford said he and the Matap guild members brought in from abroad would take down Seo Jin-Wook last night.
He was supposed to contact her if he succeeded, but no news reached her.
“Huh? Guild Master, you clocked in early.”
The surprised secretary immediately offered her tea upon arriving.
She shook her head.
“It’s okay, so stay out.”
“Yes, Guild Master. About today’s schedule…”
“As I said yesterday, keep it cleared up.”
She couldn’t get her hands on anything else.
After the secretary left, she was seriously lost in thought again.
‘I wouldn’t need to worry about it. There is no way it would fail.’
The hunters, who had been mobilized because of Seo Jin-Wook, were more than enough human resources to deal with only one SS-Rank.
But nevertheless…
‘Why am I so anxious?’
One side of her chest felt heavy and uncomfortable, as if she had an upset stomach.
It felt like she made a big mistake.
Because of the ominous feeling that filled her head, she became slightly dizzy.
She recalled her decision to join hands with Matap and provide them with as much information as she could.
‘No, I had no choice but to do this.’
She persuaded herself and justified her choice.
‘I’m certain Seo Jin-Wook killed Kim Kyung-Rok!’
The data submitted by the Matap only proved the identity of Dideric van Dyke, but there was no evidence that Seo Jin-Wook requested it.
Nevertheless, Seo Moon-Ga-In firmly believed in her conjecture.
‘Since he took care of Kim Kyung-Rok, his next target must be me. I’m sure he’ll one day swing his sword at me. This is just preemptive defense. I have no other choice!’
She strongly denied that it was due to the desire to suppress the growth of the Celestial Dragon.
She also turned a blind eye to the anxiety that filled up just below her throat.
‘Why is it taking so long to get rid of Seo Jin-Wook when he’s just a single person?’
At that moment, her terminal rang.
It was the secretary outside the door.
‘I told him to cancel today’s schedule…!’
She dissatisfiedly took the call.
“What is it?”
“Guild Master, there is a request for a meeting. He said he had an appointment in advance, but it’s not on your schedule….”
“I told you to empty today’s schedule. Turn the person away.”
The secretary spoke in a hesitant voice.
“He says his name is Arthur Clifford.”
As soon as she heard the name, Seo Moon-Ga-In got up from her seat.
A smile filled with joy spread across her face.
She shouted.
“Let him in immediately!”
“Yes, understood.”
Seo Moon-Ga-In felt a deep sense of relief, causing her to sigh.
Her heart thumped.
Instead of the anxiety that disappeared in an instant, a slight excitement arose within.
‘Yeah, there’s no way he could fail.’
In return for handing over Seo Jin-Wook’s information, Matap proposed continuous support to and cooperative relationship with the Destruction Blade guild.
It was a sweet offer for Seo Moon-Ga-In, who planned to weaken the Celestial Dragon Guild and eat up their existing rights after Seo Jin-Wook disappeared. She even accepted it without much thought.
It was a win-win deal for both parties involved, considering it was intended for the Matap to show its presence in the Korean market with the Destruction Blade at the forefront.
‘Is he here to discuss the details before returning to England?’
While she was thinking, it dawned on her.
‘… Wait a minute.’
The liaison between the Matap and the Destruction Blade was, for sure, discussed in secret.
‘Why did he come here at this hour in an official way?’
Even during their first encounter, the two chose a time when they had no eyes on them.
That was to prevent information from leaking out to the media or the industry.
‘And if it’s an official visit, why is he here alone?’
He didn’t bring any secretaries with him.
Drip.
She started to perspire.
The tension quickly made her tighten her body. Adrenaline pumped in, and her thoughts ran quicker. Her lungs began to hurt as if they were frozen as a chill passed through her spine.
The head that had been clouded by the joy of having finished with Seo Jin-Wook became clear again.
‘Why did he make a witness by making sure he was seen?’
There was only one possible reason.
‘To make evidence that the meeting between Arthur Clifford and I took place at this time, at this place!’
All those speculations led to a single conclusion.
‘That man is an impostor!’
It could have been an overthought worry or an erroneous conclusion.
However, Seo Moon-Ga-In believed in her judgment.
So who’s going to approach her disguised as Arthur Clifford?
Seo Jin-Wook was the only one who could do that.
‘What if Seo Jin-Wook indeed… Shook them all off and ran away? What if he went beyond that and even figured out the link between the Matap and me?’
If he tried to assassinate her in a one-on-one encounter, there was no chance of her winning.
Seo Moon-Ga-In, who quickly finished her calculations, checked the CCTV on the wall.
The man with Arthur Clifford’s face was already on an elevator and was swiftly approaching the Guild Master’s room on the top floor.
‘First of all, we can’t run into each other here!’
Seo Moon-Ga-In decided to retreat and immediately pulled up Mana from her body.
The blue mist gradually turned red, invoking her unique skill.
[Space Leap (Rank: SS)]
Seo Moon-Ga-In, who leaped through space, disappeared from the office without a trace.
The unique skill of an Awakened had a tremendous effect compared to skills of a similar type.
Her skill was triggered faster than the short-range teleportation magic, Blink, allowing her to quickly move deep into the building’s basement. The Mana consumed in the process was much less than Teleport, a long-distance teleportation magic spell.
Paht!
The place where she reappeared was in her secret haven located in the basement of the building.
There was no physical entrance to the room since it was blocked by thick magic metal all around.
It was also impossible to break in with movement-type magic as it was surrounded by a special barrier with a de-spell property.
The only person who could access that place was Seo Moon-Ga-In, with the teleportation skills of a non-magic-type.
Gulp!
She chugged the potion stocked inside her bunker to refill the power she consumed, then equipped various artifacts as fast as she could.
Even at that moment, her eyes were focused on the security camera.
If that man were really Arthur Clifford, he would confirm her absence and call her on the secret line.
But if he were fake, he would show different behavior.
*
“This way, please.”
The man got off the elevator with the worker who guided him.
The secretary knocked, but there was no response from within.
“Uh… Guild Master?”
The secretary was baffled.
The Guild Master suddenly disappeared after ordering him to let him in immediately.
He’s hesitating because he couldn’t simply open the door as he wished to.
“Hah.”
Suddenly, the man covered in Westerner’s disguise burst out laughing.
He took a glimpse into the scene beyond the closed door.
“She’s quick to sense things.”
The secretary, unable to grasp the situation, looked at him.
At that moment…
Paht!
The man disappeared from the top floor in an instant.
Right after that, he reappeared somewhere else.
Paht!
“Arrrrgh!”
It was the bunker where Seo Moon-Ga-In hid.
Arthur Clifford– no, Seo Jin-wook appeared in the room amid a flash and suddenly swung the devil’s sword at her.
“Gasp!”
Seo Moon-Ga-In managed to avoid being severely injured by the purple sword energy, but it still sliced into her shoulder deeply in the process.
If she hadn’t equipped the artifact, instead of her shoulder, her head might have been cut off instead.
Her head spun.
“H-how?!”
Seo Jin-Wook, who suddenly appeared at that place, looked like a ghost in the eyes of the Seo Moon-Ga-In.
She had no idea that even the barriers prepared against leap magic could be bypassed by those who could see the Mana pattern.
‘I have to run!’
The question didn’t last long.
Paht!
A light flashed from Seo Jin-Wook’s empty left hand.
Without any time to figure out who he was, Seo Moon-Ga-In once again performed her unique skill.
[Space Leap]
Paht!
The air that enveloped her threw up Seo Moon-Ga-In again a few hundred meters away. A woman in combat stance appeared on the roof of one of the buildings lined As soon as she stepped on the ground, she quickly took in a potion to stop bleeding her shoulder and once again invoked her skill.
[Space Leap]
Paht!
Seo Moon-Ga-In repeatedly activated her skill, causing her to repeatedly flashed in and out of space.
After she sustained her leaps with the help of potions, she had to be evacuated to a faraway place.
It was an empty warehouse that had been identified in advance in case of emergency.
‘He wouldn’t be able to chase me all the way here.’
Gulp!
While filling up her Mana using a potion, she felt a strange sensation like bugs were crawling all over her body.
She hurriedly took her mouth off the glass bottle she was drinking. That sensation was a harbinger of a potion shock.
‘It’s dangerous if I take any more.’
She sat on the floor and continued to think.
‘Now that I’m inside, I can’t be seen by satellites or drones. I’m also too far to be chased with [Penetration] and [Trailseeker] magic. He can’t come after me.’
Seo Moon-Ga-In was relieved.
However, she was just over only one crisis at that moment.
‘How do I deal with it? Should I get in touch with Arthur Clifford first? How did he let him go, that stupid bastard?!’
She couldn’t even imagine that they all died at the hands of Seo Jin-Wook.
As she urgently tried to contact him with her terminal.
Paht!
An unbelievable scene unfolded in front of her eyes.
“Uh…”
Her voice trembled.
“How?!”
Seo Moon-gain didn’t know that the light flashed from Seo Jin-Wook’s hand just before fleeing from the bunker was magic named [Locate Creature]. It was a rare spell that only the members of the Matap would know.
She didn’t even know that a mark had been engraved with Mana on her body when it was invoked and that she was sending a magical signal to him that could be traced no matter how far she got away.
Step by step, he approached slowly.
“W-w-wait!”
She attempted to cast Space Leap again, but she lacked Mana.
“Listen to me! This is a misunderstanding!”
Looking at her like that, Seo Jin-Wook thought.
Whatever the motivation that drove her to work with Arthur Clifford to get rid of him was, he didn’t want to know; he didn’t need to know.
He opened his lips and quietly recited a spell.
[Enhanced Gravity Field]
Rumbleee!
Hundreds of times of the natural gravitational force instantly pressed down on the body of Seo Moon-Ga-In.
She fell to the ground and resisted, but she couldn’t lift her body.
“Euuup!”
She was enduring it with the Mana that was concentrated all over her body, but she wouldn’t last long that way.
She’s braced herself for potion shock and puts the bottle she had in her hand to her mouth.
At that moment, running away and surviving was her top priority.
But then.
Shatter!
Although the glass bottle containing the potion was also a much stronger artifact than Earth’s materials, it couldn’t overcome the magic, causing it to shatter.
“N…o….”
The shadow of Seo Jin-Wook loomed over her body.
Crush!
The pain that penetrated her heart was the last feeling that Seo Moon-Ga-In felt in her life.
*
After burning the body of Seo Moon-Ga-In, I contacted Secretary Kim through a secret line.
– Yes, Guild Master.
I gave him a simple and brief instruction.
“I just sent you a list. It’s a selection of hunters from the Destruction Blade guild. Try scouting them on a condition similar to what we’ve offered to other hunters so far.”
By the condition similar to what was offered, it meant a generous reward even by global standards.
Nowadays, I didn’t give the Celestial Dragon stake when recruiting a hunter of A-Rank or higher but instead offered a huge amount of money and items that they couldn’t refuse.
I had enough money to rot away.
“Scouting will begin in three days. There will be a lot of information to secure and prepare, so I’m just letting you know in advance.”
– Yes, sir. By the way, Guild Master. There are some founders of Destruction Blade on this list, right? They won’t be moved easily.
“Three days from now, they will have a reason to move.”
Three days was enough for the Guild Master to be confirmed missing and rumors to spread among the hunters.
– … Yes, sir.
As if he had sensed something, Secretary Kim hung up.
‘Now, then.’
The new Guild Master of the Matap Guild, who would succeed Arthur Clifford, would enter the Shepherd 2 Dungeon to suck out the gold until the end, but what he would find would only be a huge pit where the sacred beast was.
Since there was no reason to keep the Gate anymore, the highly unstable dungeon would close.
I had put an end to the British breaks, secured the sacred beast, and got rid of Seo Moon-Ga-In in the process.
‘Should I return to my original duties now?’
That meant I would proceed with the process to prepare for future crises by progressing on achievement quests.
I was going to borrow Adam’s hand again.
But then.
“Requesting location information of an Awakened.”
I thought of him and asked the system, but the answer returned was the same that time again.
– Target not found within the dimension.
The system only identified the locations of the listed aliens in the same dimension.
If it’s a case where he had left our world through any methods, including entering a dungeon, it didn’t inform the location information.
‘He still must not have come out of the dungeon.’
Adam’s last known location was the undiscovered Gate located abroad.
‘I don’t know what’s going on, but it must be getting longer.’
I decided to wait a few more days for him.
*
Contrary to Seo Jin-wook’s expectations, the alien who borrowed Adam Abrams’s identity didn’t remain in the dungeon.
He went back to his home dimension for a while by stopping through a few dungeons.
Because of the imposed toll fee upon entering a tutorial world, the possibility of him escaping to another dimension was completely ruled out from Seo Jin-Wook’s head.
It was a misunderstanding that was possible since he was not aware of how many experience points Adam owned.
“Have you summoned me?”
Adam, who returned to his home dimension, tossed away his human form disguise and returned to his original form.
The scholar who opened the door and entered politely lowered himself and paid Adam respect.
He was lying on the floor, and Adam, who was calmly greeted in a chair, was looking like a giant bipedal mammal covered with white fur. His height, which was about three meters, was similar to when he was in human form. The outline of his body was round and full of flesh, while her face looked like a combination between a bear and a raccoon.
“Take a seat and make yourself comfortable.
The scholar wagged his thick tail slightly to show that he was grateful. He then sat on a chair and faced Adam.
“Did you finish your extrinsic research well as you wished?”
“No, it’s still in progress. I will return to that dimension soon.”
Although it meant that he would take longer than expected, the scholar did not add any opinion to his student’s choice.
If he made that choice, so be it.
The authority to evaluate what Adam had decided did not exist to the ‘class’ that the scholar belonged to.
“Yes, I understand.”
What the scholar could evaluate was only the achievement of Adam’s learning.
There was one more thing that Seo Jin-Wook didn’t know about Adam.
As already revealed, he expressed himself with the word ‘student’ because the exact concept didn’t exist on Earth.
Thanks to highly advanced genetic engineering technology, every being of the Yuncan species was born from an artificial womb. They already had academic memories according to the purpose of their lives from the moment they’re born. To learn something after they’re born meant two things.
One was that they were noble enough to devote part of their lives to learning.
The other meant that the contents they needed to learn were so complex, advanced, and vast that they couldn’t be contained in similar memories.
“There’s one reason I called you.”
Adam spoke to the scholar, who was his teacher.
“I heard that your knowledge of rare creatures is incomparable, is that so?”
He accessed species information about some aliens through the system.
However, the word in the system’s description was a species that he had never seen before, even with considerable alien species knowledge.
After returning to his parent dimension, he looked into their species database, which was stored in protein form instead of electrical signals, but he couldn’t find anything at all.
It was unusual.
“So, I wanted to ask thee.”
Adam brought up the question.
“What is the species called ‘Mercadius’ like?”
The scholar’s face stiffened coldly.

chapters.title: Chapter 104
chapters.content:
Fighting Fire with Fire
“What is it?”
Adam asked, noticing the sudden change in his facial expression.
The scholar couldn’t hide his surprise. He stroked the beard on his cheeks as he pondered.
“… I take it that perhaps you have heard of the species’ name through the system.”
It was an accurate conjecture.
“That’s right.”
An odd light lingered in the eyes of Adam as he answered his teacher.
The scholar had inferred that far by only hearing its name.
“So, it means that even simple information such as the name of the species can’t be identified unless it’s through the system?”
“That is right.”
The scholar continued to explain with a shaken gaze.
“Before I expound on the requested information, I wish to inquire on one thing. Did the system mention that the species was currently residing in our world, the dimension of Yuncans?”
“That does not seem to be the case.”
As if he was genuinely relieved, the scholar sighed deep.
Adam’s curiosity was inflating much bigger as he watched his reactions.
“It seems that I would need to require an explanation at this point, yes?”
The scholar spoke while bowing down as if it was much obliged.
“The reason why the information is not registered in our database is that there is no biological evidence that it exists. Blood sample, body hair, skin tissue, nor even a small division of a gene remains.”
Adam frowned.
“You mean to say it is considered a mythical species? But it must be an existing species.”
Although the system could hold back information, it didn’t lie.
“It’s as you said. The evidence that it isn’t an imaginary species is the system itself. As coincidences and chances overlapped, their existence was revealed. It was during the process of an Awakened from another world questioning the system. Only after the information about a species called ‘Mercadius’ in that world had been shared did we come to know their species.”
It was an explanation that exactly matched the process by which Adam learned of its name.
“But shouldn’t a witness exist?”
“A witness certainly exists, but there is no record of having confirmed its true form.”
“Hmm?”
“They are said to be able to transform into anything. They usually turn into the native species of a dimension and mix in with them. No Awakened can see through their camouflage, and all skills are futile. Only the system can discern its identity.”
“They hide among other world’s species?”
There was a being that came to Adam’s mind.
Although he had never faced them himself, he knew of a famous being that continued its existence in that manner.
“It is similar to a parasitic being. It’s like a leech that goes around tutorial dimensions and causes chaos. I heard that there is a being that toys around the weak and treats it as a game while it refuses to proceed to the main quest itself.”
Adam spoke of the immortal, Angelica.
She was a parasitic creature that avoided species that had started the main quest since they weren’t easy and only preyed on the weak tutorial species as they lacked knowledge.
But the scholar shook his head in disagreement.
“The first discovery of that parasitic being was only a few thousands of years ago. But it is said the record of a species called ‘Mercadius’ dates back to the ‘lost age.'”
Adam’s jaw dropped as if he couldn’t believe it.
“You mean to say that records were found even in the remains of the Sebrarian Empire?”
“That is correct.”
The rarely found traces of the old Empire in dungeons-
The study of interpreting the records had developed competitively at each dimension.
“In imperial records, Mercadius was described by the circle of eternity, a cursed wanderer, a being who breeds in spirit instead of flesh, the advocate of apocalypse…”
Adam frowned.
“Apocalypse?”
“That is right.”
The scholar carefully continued speaking, recalling memories.
“It is not clear whether the species is related to the fall of the Empire. However, after that event, there is a tale that circulated from the new-born civilization and species.”
“What is that?”
“The world where the species is found will soon face an inevitable fate of destruction. It means to say its presence is a sign of an approaching apocalypse.”
“… ?!”
Adam’s gaze deepened as he heard those words.
“Does it become a demon or something? You mean that it destroys everything and kills everyone?”
“There is no record of destruction or massacre by its own hands. However, the empirical knowledge that the world in which they were observed is destroyed has been passed down. It’s hard to tell whether Mercadius was involved in the process…”
“At least there were no exceptions, right? They don’t know exactly why or how, but once they are observed, they’ll soon face damnation?”
“That is correct.”
It was a ridiculous tale, but he couldn’t just let it pass.
Because that race, right at that moment, resided on Earth.
“The apocalypse must mean the annihilation of life instead of concepts such as the collapse of time and space, yes?”
“That is right.”
“Is this a story with legitimacy?”
“It is information that is taken much seriously from the Union. In fact, considering that there was a member dimension that suddenly collapsed in their long history…”
“Perhaps they might have secured something to prove the connection.”
After the scholar stepped down, Adam was lost in deep thought.
It was an ancient species that had been on the records since the time of the Sebrarian Empire.
Why was such a being staying on Earth?
‘Is apocalypse the goal of Mercadius? Or, even if that is not the purpose itself, the effect that followed the event of Mercadius’ appearance is… apocalypse?’
Looking at the Union’s attitude, it wasn’t a story that was vain.
In that age where the Empire had disappeared, the Union was the longest-lasting organization.
‘If that’s all true, it means that Earth is fated to be destroyed sooner or later.’
There was no way that the tutorial dimension could prevent the ‘entity’ that couldn’t be stopped even by the main quest dimensions.
‘Why would such a being show interest in Seo Jin-Wook?’
The moment he heard the abilities that Seo Jin-Wook described, he expected the fact that the opponent was a very dangerous being.
However, since he had also heard the scholar’s words, he realized that it was a threat that was much deadlier and more enormous than he imagined.
“Hmm.”
His worries deepened.
At that point, he could pull out of the dimension called Earth.
But there was a reason why he couldn’t do so that time.
‘Seo Jin-Wook was a promising candidate for a successor.’
That was the key to leading his long-cherished desire into action.
‘But the identity of the enemy is something too powerful and too dangerous for me to rush in.’
Adam was well aware that his life weighed more than only one of the Yuncan species’.
He soon reached a conclusion.
‘Yes, if it’s too dangerous for me to intervene on my own, I’ll borrow the other guys’ hands.’
He quickly ran the calculations.
‘It is said that the Union knows about Mercadius. Whatever the effect may be, the extinction of life from a dimension is the worst-case scenario for the Union as well.’
What the Union was trying to seek was the entry of more dimensions into the main quest.
Mercadius was a dangerous being that went head-on against their goals.
‘Mercadius is on Earth where six observers have been dispatched? If the Union had known, there’s no way that they’d let him be!’
Adam was sure.
‘That being on Earth is an illegal immigrant.’
Species in Main Quest that sneaked in, avoiding the eyes of the Union.
A plan began to take shape in his head.
‘There was a Ghenut among the observers.’
He thinks of the alien disguised in the form of a toy poodle.
The species that suffered from a chronic lack of experience points overfocused on the achievement of the arrest of illegal aliens and earning points. It even drove the innocent Seo Jin-Wook to the corner, assuming that he was an alien.
‘If they knew that such a being had snuck in on Earth, they will immediately start a raid operation. Yes, the Union is the only armed group at this point that can handle such an inter-dimensional threat!’
Adam displayed a satisfied smile on his mouth.
The next action to be taken was simple.
He got up from his seat and murmured.
“Then… Shall I leak some information to their side?”
He would get rid of Mercadius with the help of the Union.
*
“Ah, are we cleaning up here again today?”
I reserved a day and entered the gray-earthed dungeon together with Nate and Hibiki.
It’s the same dungeon where we transferred the seedlings together and regularly cleaned up the monsters that rushed in.
“Grrrr!”
“Kaaaaaaaaaaaaah!
As we crossed the gate, we saw many monsters clumped like black dots beyond the horizon.
The number had increased significantly compared to the last time I came there.
They had become very irritated, perhaps because of the overpopulation as opposed to the area of land. They were attacking and even eating each other.
Monster fragments and bones rolled around on the ground. In addition to the corpses I made last time, their bodily fluids had been absorbed and mummified.
Hibiki spoke while witnessing the chaotic scene.
“If a number of them rush here a bit more… It will be like the density of the population in the subway during rush hour.”
“Yeah, we need to reduce the number of creatures once in a while before that happens. We need to prevent them from damaging the trees.”
Nate, who received my signal, rolled up his sleeves as if he was preparing for work.
The Spirit that ran the security system was still asleep.
“Come on, let’s finish this as fast as we could today as well.”
Nate then clapped his hands twice in the air while saying those words.
Swoosh!
A heavy gust blew, and a humongous black dragon was summoned from the sky.
It cast a shadow that loomed over a group of monsters on the ground.
The moment they looked up to the sky…
Kwaaaaaa!
The river of fire breathed out by the dragon violently incinerated the ground.
In every place where the storm of flames passed, burnt monsters rolled around.
[Fire Buster!]
[Lightning Vortex!]
[Energy Storm!]
Hibiki conjured several spells at the same time.
Flames exploded at the points where she pointed, a python-like current twisted its body and slithered towards their opponents, and a storm of blue light swept through the lands.
The energy of different properties intertwined and led to larger explosions.
Boo-boo-boo-boom!
Amid the mass extermination, I spread [Stardust Wings] and flew up and scattered purple sword energy.
After a while, all of the monsters had been eradicated beyond the point of salvation.
“Huh? It’s blooming a flower?”
The seedlings planted in the center of the dungeon had grown more in the meantime.
Nate smiled brightly as he looked at the buds that covered the branches.
“If the flowers have bloomed…”
Hibiki continued as if she had remembered my explanation.
“That means there’s really not much time left.”
I agreed with her.
“The next time we come, I think we’ll have to stay here for some time.”
The moment when it would bear fruits was just right around the corner.
“Now, before that.”
I approached the pond where Igras-Sho’s statue was located.
The artificial pond hidden between the seedlings had changed its appearance.
The huge hole that could easily bury 2-3 large trolls was so dried up that the bottom used to be seen in the previous dungeon.
But at that very moment…
“Jin-Wook. Over there… Won’t the water overflow?”
Along the border of the pond, the gray land was consistent like mud.
“Oh, yes, it seems so.”
The holy water, beyond just filling up the pond to the brim, was overflowing.
That meant more than enough monster corpses had been offered.
I took out seven cards from my arms while looking at it.
“Now, with this, what we have to do here is done.”
Hibiki looked at it as if she didn’t understand.
It was seven SS-Class magic cards.
Mastery skill cards that I secured for that day but didn’t hand over to Hibiki.
Splash!
I threw seven cards into the pond all at once.
Flash!
The holy water that filled the pond turned dark, and soon, it was sucked into the card as if the black fog was lifted.
As the holy water turned transparent and clear…
Rumbleeee!
The water level began to lower.
‘I expected it, but the holy water consumption is higher than upgrading S-Class cards.’
After a while, I took out the seven cards submerged in the lowered water surface.
Hibiki’s eyes grew bigger when she saw its effect.
[Fire Mastery (Rank: SSS)]
[Ice Mastery (Rank: SSS)]
[Lightning Mastery (Rank: SSS)]
[Earth Mastery (Rank: SSS)]
[Summon Mastery (Rank: SSS)]
[Enchant Mastery (Rank: SSS)]
[Universal Mastery (Rank: SSS)]
Her jaw dropped.
“No way…”
I nodded my head.
“Yes, let’s upgrade all your skill slots today.”
I pondered around my thoughts while handing the card to her.
From that point on, it was an area that she had never experienced in the previous life.
There were only three types of SSS-Class magic mastery that Hibiki had mastered in her previous life: Fire, Ice, and Lightning.
Until the last minute, the remaining four masteries were only up to SS-Class and S-Class.
That was because the supply of magic cards was that rare.
‘Upgrading all seven masteries to SSS-Class is an order that even I don’t know will be created.’
And…
‘If I get an SSS-Class magic card one day.’
It could be evolved into an EX-Class card.
“Come on, now.”
When I urged her, Hibiki infused Mana into the card.
And.
Boosh!
The moment Mana sparkled in Hibiki’s hand-
“… ?!”
I thought even my senses were malfunctioning.
Everything stopped instantly.
‘… What?!’
The shadow of all things in the dungeon disappeared.
Nate’s eyes froze as he was looking at the card that turned to a skill with interest. He stopped like a mannequin with his lips open as if he was trying to say something.
The glow that lingered on top of Hibiki’s hand froze. She became fixed like a still image just before she exclaimed with a half nervous and half excited face.
‘How about the devil’s sword?!’
That day, I left the devil’s sword about 1km away from the pond.
Compared to before, the divine power that was flowing out of the pond was… To borrow his expression, it was spreading everywhere ‘like it was going to boil the atmosphere until it was fatal.’
It said it was impossible to approach any closer than that.
I looked into the air where I left my sword.
Then in that space-
Tssssss!
As if it were burning a living animal, black smoke was flowing out of the devil’s sword.
At that moment, when time seemed to have been paused, movements were happening around me and the devil’s sword, as it was originally a still object.
The moment I saw that…
– You don’t have to panic.
A whisper that heavily echoed my head seeped in.
The source where it was emitted from was in the direction of the sacred beast, which took a pond’s shape.
“… !”
I had never heard that the sacred beast had intellect.
Rather than a creature with free will, I believed it to be only a temple made of bodily fluids and flesh.
Telepathic messages continued to appear in my head while I was baffled.
– The great being was greatly pleased and satisfied with your offerings. Therefore, he has a deep interest in thee, but unfortunately, it is too much to convey his will to the place where you stay, so the blessing will be given upon thee by changing it into an acceptable form.
I could barely open his mouth.
I forced my body to move and for my lips to spill out words in the space where everything had frozen.
“… What do you mean?”
– You will see it soon.
Shortly after that, the world, where the shades disappeared, began to turn black entirely.
The scene of the holy water darkening was reenacted on the scale of the dungeon.
The sacred beast, which was fading out of my sight, leaked out telepathy into my mind again.
– A buoy that will be swept away by the waves of time, a mere mortal like you. A weak and vain man… Had attracted the interest of a great being…
Telepathy was accompanied by a mental curve similar to an exclamation.
– You, who gained his attention, is nothing but truly…
The next mental wave was mixed with a strange echo.
– … Foolish and naive.
At that moment, everything around me disappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 105
chapters.content:
Igras-Sho
Surrounding me was riffling, thick darkness.
I opened my eyes in the dark shadow.
‘… This place is?!’
Near me, neither Nate, Hibiki, the devil’s sword… nor the sacred beast that took the pond’s shape was around.
The dungeon with the gray field had disappeared, and only darkness existed.
‘Forced physical teleportation? Or, mind interference? Or did the whole dungeon temporarily turn into a sacred place?’
The thing that disrupted my chaotic flow of thought was an object that caught my eyes.
‘It’ appeared eerily, pushing the darkness away.
The fluttering shadow was torn in between like a torrent, and at the center was a white flesh that stole my attention.
It was difficult to estimate the size since I could not measure the distance between us.
‘… It’s changing!’
Like the plain marble blocks that were carved out by an outline and shades, it turned into a detailed statue.
The shape, which only looked like a lump of white flesh, began to change sophistically.
At the same time, I realized the illusion I had.
‘It isn’t that its form is changing, but my cognitive abilities are becoming clearer.’
[The Successor’s Eyes] helped me overcome cognitive impairment and see reality as clearly as possible.
As a result, I was able to see a creature in a familiar shape instead of a chunk of flesh.
The flesh, which was the body, had seven thin white arms that extend symmetrically from side to side.
The perfect symmetry was disconnected at the end. There was a blunt mark in the frontmost, where the right arm should be attached as if it had been torn off.
There was a head at the center of the body that was too similar to that of humans. Like a ghost, there were no eyes, nose, and mouth but simply a face covered with bare skin.
‘It doesn’t exactly match the appearance of the idol, but…’
It would have been strange not to know who it was with that kind of look.
‘Igras-Sho!’
It was a being that was adored as a god in many dimensions that had finished the tutorial.
The darkness that filled that space was flowing from the base of Igras-Sho’s severed arm.
Even at that moment, the god seemed to be constantly losing parts of itself.
‘Why would a god bring me here?!’
I remembered what the sacred beast had said.
A great being would bless me in an acceptable form.
‘Does it mean that I can connect with the god by only offering that much of monsters?’
Something’s wrong with that.
Tension filled my entire body instinctively.
At that moment, my head was filled with questions. However, I had no time to organize them.
“… !”
The darkness began to press on me without warning.
The boundaries between my five senses then collapsed and converged. In the storm of collapsing senses, I heard scents, tasted sounds, and touched the fluttering shadow.
Beyond that tangled senses, the darkness licked my skin and whispered.
You have good eyes, don’t you, boy?
It knew that my eyes accurately captured it.
The god’s whisper had a jasmine scent that was viscous like honey.
Once more, it continued as if it was interested in me.
But you’re not fully ripe yet. Is it too much to use you as my hands and feet?
My thoughts became more complicated when I encountered the heavy echo.
What the hell did it want from me?
A thing like connecting to a god couldn’t be that easy, by common sense. I had only offered thousands of monsters… What would be its intention? I had a headache because my thoughts turned heavy. I wanted to rip its head off like a butterfly without a head. I had seen it dried up, tangled in a spider’s web. It’s light as paper, and the head flew away somewhere. If one were to eat the head first, the body would be drained of fluids and dried up. If my strength drained and flowed, without being able to escape, I would stay there for a long time, stay some more, and how much longer? I would curse them, curse them all. Terrible revenge on all those who had exiled me there… I would bring them… Someday, I would–
“K-ugh!”
In a hurry, I bounced off all the foreign substance-like ideas that had been digging into my mind.
“Huff… Huff!”
I gasped with rapid breathing like a distressed man who barely swam out of the water after drowning.
I could feel the unpleasantness of the body and mind being dragged down heavily.
‘What was that just now?!’
It felt like another being swept into my soul like a tide and mixed it up messily.
I had barely managed to resist and defended myself before crossing the last line and being completely taken over.
And a step behind, the system message rang out.
– … S… u… cces… sso… r’s Eyes resists to [?????? (Rank: ?????)]. Resistance effect is not perfect because of overw… hel… m… ing p… ow… er…
System messages were delivered not only slow but also felt distant and faint, like static radio waves.
I had cold sweats pouring, but the darkness once again giggled as if it were having fun.
Your soul is durable and tough. Isn’t that admirable?
Only then did I feel the distance between Igras-Sho and me.
The darkness between the two was as wide and endless as the universe in that vast space.
The great being kept whispering to me.
You truly are a child worthy of my attention… In a piece of time and space that has been divided into a myriad of numbers. I want to keep you around for a long time, but it’s not the right time, so I’ll give you a simple gift instead.
The moment I understood its meaning, I wanted to shout with all my might.
I wanted to scream that I didn’t need it, but then.
Shh!
My hand lifted itself, and at the end of it, a warm and damp sensation lingered.
At the very next moment, there was a burning pain in my fingers.
I couldn’t even scream in the deep darkness as I felt the torment of my nerves burning.
While I was in that state, the darkness tossed a word to me.
Three times. I’ll give you three chances to call my name. Put it on your tongue and lips at the most desperate moment.
In the pain of my fingers crushing and turning into ashes, I gritted my teeth.
I didn’t exactly know what that suggestion meant, but it sounded sinister and ominous.
With a subtle whisper, it greeted me farewell.
Eventually, we’ll see each other again.
And the darkness tossed me off.
*
“… !”
The chaotic air in the dungeon surrounded me as if to smack me.
“Huh? Jin-Wook, what’s wrong?”
I was back inside the gray-earthed dungeon.
I think I knew how my expression looked even if I couldn’t see it.
Nate, who had been frozen like a mannequin, was moving again and was gazing at me with concern.
Hibiki, who had her eyes closed and looked at the list of newly available orders, also noticed a strange atmosphere.
“Is there something wrong?”
“…”
I took a deep breath and organized my perplexed mind.
“… No, It’s nothing.”
The moment they saw me doing that for the first time, much deeper worry cast on the two’s faces.
I barely caught myself in the middle of my terror.
“How about the change of the seven cards into skills? Everything’s going great, right?”
When I returned to my usual way of speaking, Hibiki nodded and smiled as if she was relieved.
“Yes, mastery skill of seven types. It completed upgrading everything to SSS-Rank.”
“Good, you’ll have to get used to the new spells for a while, so practice hard… Well, for you, Hibiki, you’ll do just well without me telling you this.”
Hibiki nodded her head with eyes full of motivation.
I turned my head to bring back the devil’s sword that was floating in the distance.
As I flicked my finger-
Swish!
Instantly, the sword flew towards me.
As soon as I held the handle, the devil’s sword gave off a loud mental wave.
‘You… you… you… What happened in that short time?!’
As I remembered the sheath of the devil’s sword producing black smoking, I answered the question with a question.
“I should be the one to ask that. Did anything change in you?”
However, the devil’s sword wasn’t aware at all that time had stopped, and it seemed to not feel any abnormalities in its state.
It replied with a fuss.
‘Don’t change the topic. The problem right now is not me but you! I’m asking you, why in the hell do I feel sacred power from your body!’
“Sacred power?”
Knowing that I was talking with the devil’s sword, Nate and Hibiki, who were talking with each other, turned their heads because of a suddenly raised tone.
‘It’s much weaker than that sacred beast, but I can feel it. That unpleasant sensation!’
“No, wait. No way.”
I recalled that in the darkness, I felt a terrible pain in my left hand.
I moved my left arm to take a closer look at it.
‘Ahh! Don’t put it near the sword!’
The devil’s sword got surprised and acted as if it were appalled.
Ignoring its reaction, I checked my left hand.
I noticed the strange change right away.
Unbeknownst to me, I swore.
“Damn it, what is this?!”
Red marks were aligned side by side on my left index finger.
There were three spot-shaped scars in the middle of the dark red circle.
When the snakes on my wrist didn’t respond automatically, I performed recovery magic myself, but of course, it didn’t disappear.
The two of them approached me with worried faces.
“Huh? That!”
Pointing at the marks left on my hand, Nate spoke.
“Jin-Wook, did you get bitten by a bug?”
“… Bug?”
“Yeah, I know a bug bite when I see one.”
Nate, who was bitten by all kinds of things in his younger years as he lived in poverty, answered confidently.
“Yeah, this is definitely a bite mark from something.”
He carefully looked at the scar and spoke.
“Hmm, it is usually spiders that leave a scar like this.”
Spider.
Crack.
As I gritted my teeth, I recalled the last thing that the god whispered to me from the dark.
‘Three times. I will give you three chances to call my name.’
And the three scars that were imprinted on my finger.
It wasn’t too hard to guess their relationship.
*
“Hey! Have you been well?”
The one to enter my office door without any notice or knock was a hairy man who was 3 meters tall.
“… Ah, have you arrived?”
I greeted Adam, who came back from a few days of outings.
He wondered when he saw a slightly subdued expression.
“What’s with your face? I have brought very good news to you.”
For some reason, he looked a little excited.
However, he must have felt a trace of worry on my face. He tilted his head.
“Did something happen?”
“… Something did happen.”
“Is it bad?”
“That’s the problem. I can’t discern if this is a good thing or a bad thing.”
“Tell me about it. I’m called an information consultant for a reason. I’ll help you in any way that I can help you with!”
To be honest, his suggestion made me open my ears.
Human beings on Earth, including myself, had little direct contact with the divine being in the previous life.
The same went for other dimensions that were proceeding with the tutorial.
All I knew about the gods were their name, characteristics, uses, and the meaning of traces revealed through dungeons, like the case of Shepherd 2 dungeon.
However, it was said that the dimensions undergoing the main quest were more deeply intertwined with the divine beings.
“What happened is…”
Adam, who listened to my explanation, first showed concern and darkened his face, then turned pale with frightening surprise, and at the end, he was excited to the point that he turned red, and the veins in his forehead and neck threatened to pop out of his neck.
“I-I-Is that true?”
“I’m not lying. I swear.”
He fumed, and with rather rough breathing, spoke out.
“No, does that make sense?!”
“I don’t understand it either.”
To a mortal who hadn’t even finished the tutorial, why would a god show such deep interest?
“What the hell did you offer them that the heavy-assed gods revealed themselves? Did you destroy a planet? You wouldn’t have carried out a massacre on Earth, so… Perhaps on a different dimension?”
“There were only thousands of monsters.”
“… Are you serious?”
“I’m serious.”
His face became stiffer.
He was lost in thought for a while before he opened his mouth again.
“First of all, it’s already great that you got to come back. Usually, the cognitive self melts and mixes up there. I already know this, but you seem to have a great skill.”
“…”
“But from now on, you have to think that you’re under some kind of probation. A self-imposed prohibition that is.”
“What do you mean?”
“From now on, never, even unconsciously, or by accident… Mention the name of the god in your mouth!”
It meant that I shouldn’t pronounce the name of Igras-Sho.
“It didn’t matter if you got a blessing corresponding to the scale of consecration. However, to have connected with god by only offering a few monsters… It means great danger. For ridiculous reasons, the god recognized and even remembered the existence of a mortal man named Seo Jin-Wook. If the Earth had been through the tutorial, he would have made you into a god.”
He continued, frowning as he pointed at my scar.
“It’s impossible right now, so he stopped only up to that point. The thing left on your finger is called holy wounds. Surely, it would be of a mechanism that if you call the name of that god, in exchange for granting a wish, the scar will disappear one by one. It means you can make up to three wishes.”
“However,” he continued.
“I recommend that you don’t use any of them. There is no guarantee how your wishes will come true… and the most tricky part is what happens in the case that you have used all three chances.”
He spoke in a heavy voice as if he were warning me.
“Nobody really knows what’s going to happen then.”
I sighed and nodded.
I agreed with him about that.
“Yeah, there would probably be no instances for me to use it.”
“Good thinking.”
Without realizing it, I turned my eyes once again toward the scars on my finger.
I thought I was caught up in something very troublesome.
“Oh, by the way!”
Adam changed the topic.
His expression lightened up a little.
“I told you I have good news!”
“Hmm, what is it?”
He replied with a smile.
“The alien you were anxiously searching for, I finally found it.”
It was good news that I didn’t expect.
“Really?”
“Yeah, I’ve checked, and he seems to have hidden at this dimension without reporting it to the union. In their books, he’s called an illegal immigrant. And the better news is…”
He laughed with his teeth revealed.
“A Union observer has decided to arrest that bastard himself!”

chapters.title: Chapter 106
chapters.content:
Ilyusha
I couldn’t understand what was going on since he skipped all the context in between and went straight to the conclusion.
“That alien is an illegal immigrant? Before that…. How did you know that he was the one out of a list of over 50 people?”
Adam grinned and replied.
“On that list, I found the one whose species is named ‘Mercadius.'”
Mercadius!
When I explained the man’s ability in Seo Gyu-Cheol’s memory to Adam, I also told him assumptions about his unique skill.
So, the proper noun in the skill name was actually the name of the species!
“And how did you learn of that?”
“It’s a trade secret. Let me just tell you that I even mobilized resources from my home dimension.”
There was no way he opened the information of every alien species on my list one by one. That’s like gambling with the points.
No, there must’ve been another way. No matter how much I thought about it, it wasn’t an option for someone whose purpose was to accumulate points.
“Anyway,”
Adam continued.
“Do you remember the dog-shelled observer? The situation is favorable to us. The target’s location seems to be in its jurisdiction. If we wait, we should be able to hear about the arrest.”
The poodle came after me, assuming that I was an alien.
It seemed quite hungry for achievements.
“Will it succeed?”
“If the Union can’t do it, then no one can. I hate to admit it, but they’re the biggest armed organization of this era.”
He continued with a relaxed smile.
“We can only wish them luck and relax.”
“…”
Without any knowledge about the Union, I had nothing to add.
I thanked him.
“I received a lot of help from you on
That included the information on the holy wound on my finger.
He was a greater help than expected, considering he even initiated the arrest of the curse’s source by leaking words to the observer.
“I assume that the price of this information would be experience points, right? How much would be enough?”
I didn’t intend to take it without paying for the information.
Adam scratched his chin and said lightly without much thought.
“A hundred thousand would be enough.”
100,000 again?
He also asked for 100,000 last time in the achievement quest that drove out the Botarch.
It wasn’t a paid subscription or something…
“Would that be enough?”
“Think of it as a benefit for regulars. I look forward to regular transactions.”
Adam laughed with a mysterious smile.
*
While waiting for good news from the Union, domestic and foreign media became rowdy.
Seo Moon-Ga-In’s disappearance quickly reached the headlines, and discussions about selecting the Destruction Blade’s new Head began immediately. The ones who were second in command that had been aiming for an opportunity to usurp her throne quickly showed their true colors and began to move.
A fierce battle for the position unfolded, and the media continuously broadcasted the entire process.
In the meantime, a small number of hunters, who were not interested in the power struggle despite being skilled, began to withdraw from the Destruction Blade one after another.
“Guild Master, more than half of hunters from the list have already decided and have signed the contract to join the Celestial Dragon.”
I nodded satisfactorily after receiving the report from Secretary Kim.
What I gave him was a list of only those who were worthy of being scouted based on my memories from the future.
“You did a great job. We won’t look good if we take out too many of them at once… So, keep being diligent but don’t rush the recruitment process. We’re not short of the workforce right now anyways.”
Thanks to the [Aurora of Stability], there were no longer any ‘very unstable’ dungeons in Korean territory, and we got some room to breathe before Clearing.
There was space for workforce management.
“Yes, understood.”
That was the end for the Destructional Blade, which became an absolute mess, but the situation of Matap, which had their leader missing as well, was worse.
Contrary to my expectations, the surviving SS-Class hunters didn’t fight for the position of Guild Master.
Shortly after losing contact with Arthur, it was said that they first checked the status of Shepherd 2 Dungeon.
‘Then, they must have confirmed the disappearance of the sacred beast.’
It was a real emergency for them.
The agent that placed Matap in their current status was the enormous wealth brought in by the magic cards.
In return for providing rewards that all the hunters would be satisfied with, they continued their reputation as the guild with an exclusive status in their country.
However, when the treasure disappeared, Matap had been torn apart, piece by piece.
From what I heard, the SS-Rank hunters got their fair share and left, and they proceeded with the preparation of a guild creation or something.
When they were asked what Arthur Clifford was doing in Korea before he went missing and why he was seen at the Destructional Blade Guild at the last minute, they only repeatedly said that they didn’t know.
They claimed that they had nothing to do with themselves since they already left the guild.
‘Yes, they can never say that he planned to hold hands with the Destruction Blade to strike me.’
On the day Arthur Clifford visited Seo Moon-Ga-In, they both went missing.
It was clear circumstantial evidence.
The media already took the bait and poured out speculations about what could have happened between the two.
The Destruction Blade, which was in chaos due to the collapse of Matap and internal conflict, remained silent as if they had promised to do so.
Due to that, rumors and speculations became even more prevalent.
Naturally, some aimed their arrows of suspicion at me.
– Isn’t this too obvious? 2 leaders among the four major guilds suddenly died and went missing this year… If you think about who would benefit the most in this situation, can’t you see the answer?
↳ Of course, it’s the Celestial Dragon.
↳ True. Seo Jin-Wook seems suspicious to my eyes as well.
There was also a lot of rebuttal to such public opinion.
– LMAO, thank you for that delusional talk from those guys up there. Don’t you know how Kim Kyung-Rok died? He died fighting Dideric van Dyke. How about Seo Moon-Ga-In? On the day she met an SSS-Rank hunter, they disappeared together. Is Seo Jin-Wook a god? Was he controlling Dideric van Dyke and Arthur Clifford from behind? Brainwashed them? Is he some omnipotent force that controls all the hunters in the world?
↳ There are kids now that talk shit whenever Seo Jin-Wook is mentioned LOOOL. All sort of bullshit happens now that he’s famous.
↳ How can they find him suspicious and bash him? Is there a hunter who can come close to his achievements? Some guilds Clear dungeons, and some hunters stopped breaks, but where in the world can you find a hunter that reversed the instability of every dungeon in Korea?
↳ They also said that their progress would slow down. Hunter on T.V. read everything from the [Analysis] information.
↳ Other countries must be foaming around their mouths LMFAO.
– Yo, wait a minute. There is no evidence that Seo Jin-Wook did the aurora of stability thin…
↳ It’s a silent agreement, LOL. Who else than Seo Jin-Wook could do that?
– Well, Celestial Dragon is on a whole new level apart from other guilds. They’re discovering dungeons like they’re just stumbling upon it these days too… They’re not in the level to mind Grand Croix or Destruction Blade anymore. Why would they harm them first when they can’t keep up even when left alone?
Despite the overwhelming public opinion, those who were skeptical of me did not disappear. It reached a point where the legal department was gathering opinions to respond seriously to it.
I told the legal department’s team leader not to waste their workforce on trivial matters.
It was because I knew that some of their voices would vanish completely soon.
A few days later, the time finally came.
*
Since morning, all the headlines had been showcasing only a single matter.
– We are announcing the revolutionary achievements of the Joint Venture (J/V) between the Celestial Dragon Guild and Danton Corporation, which have overturned common knowledge!
– They have successfully mass-produced weapon-type artifacts!
The mass-produced artifact was developed and made by the Senator’s researchers based on the blueprints I provided.
When the initial model was released to the press, media all over the world began to explode with the news.
Every channel that I switched to was showing a data screen provided by J/V.
It was a scene where a C-Class hunter injected Mana into the mass-produced artifact.
‘…This is just perfect! It’s no different from the items found in dungeons! No, it’s rather easier to use. It’s just the right size for the Earthlings’ figure!’
The interview scene where a hunter wielded a sword with the sword energy activated while shouting was broadcasted globally.
It was a solution for the lack of supply for the high demand of weapon-type artifacts has been created. It was a historical moment.
The following news reported that the innovative invention was ready for mass production and that the contract with the first customer had been completed.
– First-time production slots are supplied to all U.N. forces in TIFER-2!
They were the U.N. military’s powerful troops that were under trusteeship over some of the former North Korean territories.
For most of them who were skilled C-Rank or lower, mass-produced artifacts were the perfect supplies.
Because they had no choice but to rely entirely on mining products in dungeons, the troops had to guard the Fortress City’s outskirts only with F-Rank or E-Rank items.
If items that reliably maximized a C-Rank’s performance were supplied in bulk, there would be a great synergy effect.
When I visited the Fortress City not too long ago, my tea time with the United Nations commander under the Korean government’s introduction was not simply for personal management but to discuss the supply of artifacts.
Ring ring!
The moment when wide P.R. started to unfold in the media, I got a call in good timing.
On the line was the Senator.
“What do you think? I think this is enough publicity.”
I replied agreeably.
“It’s more than enough.”
The fact the C-Rank hunters or below composed the majority of the population didn’t only apply to the army of skilled soldiers of the United Nations.
We already knew that orders would pour in from all over the world once the items’ effects were proven in practice.
“I sent another blueprint just now.”
“I saw. I called in after checking it out.”
What I sent that day wasn’t the next design of the initial model but the third-generation model, which was beyond it.
The development of a follow-up model had already begun, so it was natural.
“The Chief Technology Officer nearly collapsed from seeing that. I guess you threw him something pretty heavy this time?”
I laughed when I heard that they seriously asked if I wasn’t actually an alien when I provided the data.
According to that new blueprint, it seemed like it would be completed a bit faster than in my previous life.
That was because it boldly omitted trials and errors.
“If we mass-produce up to the third generation, our combat efficiency will be incomparably improved.”
While we talked about our plans, the Senator’s eyes on the hologram became focused on one side.
“Hmm?”
I think he got a call from another line.
At the same time…
Beep beep! Beep!
A message from Secretary Kim also arrived.
It had a title marked urgent.
When I clicked it, a video came up.
“… Are you watching this now?”
“Yes.”
“Hmm, there’s no known gate in that area. What the hell is going on? Did the undiscovered gate go off, or is it an immediate break?”
My face stiffened for a reason different from the Senator’s worries.
Inside the hologram, there was breaking news that an unexplained explosion occurred in eastern Russia, and a giant crater was formed that was several kilometers in diameter.
After checking the coordinates, I couldn’t help but gulp.
It was the area where the observer, who was disguised as a toy poodle, resided.
*
Russian Federation, Republic of Sakha.
Hums resonated from a small cabin far from the residential area.
“Hmmm~ Hmmmm…”
The toy poodle sat on a fluffy cushion, humming in tune with a melody famous in a different dimension.
A black-haired young man who was knitting in front of the stove turned his head.
“Have you got something good going on, Ilyusha?”
Sergei, the young man, asked the small dog that had raised him since he was a baby.
Ilyusha was the name that he wanted to call it, but it had a different real name.
He could not pronounce it properly even if it told him. Hence, it simply allowed Sergei to call it whatever he wanted to.
“Is it obvious?”
The young man nodded with a pure smile.
“Yes, I’m happy because Ilyusha looks happy.”
“How can you speak so sweetly? You make me feel raising you was worth it.”
Ilyusha was an alien who found a crying baby left alone in that old cabin far from the village.
His maternal grandmother, who died of chronic disease while raising him instead of his runaway parents, was already becoming cold right next to the child.
Instead of watching which between malnutrition or hypothermia would stop the baby’s breathing first, it decided to raise the young member of the native species. The idea that it would be too quiet to stay alone for a long time on that outskirt dimension without any connection factored in its decision.
Since then, the alien had provided adequate nutrition for the human child. It even later Awakened him.
That was because it knew that his lifespan was much shorter in natural conditions compared to the alien’s.
“The reason I feel good is that–”
The toy poodle hummed and spoke.
“There’s a big case. I think I’ll get some hefty reward. If that happens, I’ll wave goodbye to this outskirt dimension.”
As soon as he heard that, he stopped fiddling with the needles.
At the same time, Sergei looked as if the sky was collapsing.
“Ilyusha… Are you going back home?”
“I have to. I can’t just keep rotting here, can I? I’m only 300 years old, and I can’t always be a slave to points and waste my youth.”
“··· Then what am I going to do?”
Hearing the words, the toy poodle laughed absurdly.
