“Jin-Wook! I was counting on you. You’ve come to our rescue!”
Nate seemed like he was about to dance.
“Oh, as expected. Of course. I believed you would find us before anyone else.”
He then mumbled.
“Wait, so they don’t even have to be taken out, do they? Hey, all of you! Get back in there!”
Swoosh!
The wind blew, and the subordinates Nate summoned were quickly sucked back into his shadow.
“Uhm… What is this situation about?”
Cautiously, the devil of the forest talked to Nate.
Nate then waved his hand as if it was nothing to worry about.
“Oh! It’s okay. Jin-Wook is on our side. You don’t have to fight him!”
He scratched his chin and corrected his words.
“… no, you shouldn’t fight him. That would be disastrous. For you.”
Only then did the devils, aiming their bows at us and surrounding us, retract their weapons.
Then they set a polite attitude and took a step back.
I spoke with a frown on my face.
“I think I will need an explanation here.”
“Oh, before that!”
Nate’s expression changed quickly, but that time he was in tears.
“We would have been in big trouble if you got here a bit later. The Roheem guys broke all of our telecommunications, preventing us from reaching out to you or the Union.”
Roheem?
That name kept being popping up.
To describe who they were, they were the race that was dispatched and formed a joint expedition team with the Celestial Dragon Guild members.
I could roughly guess what had happened.
“No way.”
My face stiffened quickly.
“Did they stab you in your back?”
Nate nodded.
“This is driving me mad.”
At the same time as I thought it was ridiculous, I felt anger rising like flames from within me.
If they were to do such a thing between Union member dimensions, they would surely be severely reprimanded.
The fact that they nevertheless put it into action meant that they had the confidence to bury it without leaving any evidence.
That was the same method the Adgon punks used.
But Roheem was… They’re punks that just weren’t even near that level.
I gritted my teeth.
“Even if they underestimated Earthlings, they went overboard with it.”
From the perspective of the Union headquarters, the Earthlings or the Roheem, considering only the individual battle capability of both species’ Awakened, were weak races that fell short of the average.
Yet even the Roheem belittled the people of Earth and plotted such a nefarious plan.
I asked Nate a question in a rather harsh tone.
“Explain to me what on earth happened.”

chapters.title: Chapter 180
chapters.content:
Trace of the Monarch (3)
Instead of standing there and talking, we decided to go into the base of the devils.
The rest of them were said to be in there.
“But they’re all in terrible shape right now…”
Nate’s expression got worse the more he talked about it.
‘This is going to drive me mad.’
While I was lost in thought, a devil stood in front of the barrier and formed a unique Mana pattern.
Looking at the scale of the Mana’s vibration, it must’ve been a magic circle set up by the Monarch-class devil in the past.
I kept the pattern that functioned as a key in mind.
Shhh!
Space distorted, and the door opened.
Beyond the barrier, there was a long passage leading to the underground.
Walking together, Nate confided about what had happened.
Their predicament’s main culprit was the species called Roheem, who formed the expedition team with them.
From the moment they first saw Earth’s hunters, they reportedly displayed an attitude that looked down on them.
I was dumbfounded, listening to it.
‘Those mediocre punks, when their strongest being has barely 60 to 70 thousand Mana…!’
Nate grunted.
“Hmph, what a pain in the ass they were. I had to put up with them even though I wanted to fight them. Hibiki explained everything to me. If that happened, it would be reported to the Union, and Jin-Wook would’ve been in trouble. So I held myself back.”
So while they were just concentrating on their work, pretending not to notice it, Hibiki seemed to have finally found a clue.
“Jin-Wook, you saw it when you walked by, right, the barrier? She said there was a small gap on it. Hibiki found it through magic. It was something that even the pretentious Roheems couldn’t find it.”
Nate spoke with pride as if it was his own achievement.
“That moment definitely humbled them down.”
They took advantage of the gap to break through the barrier.
But their method wasn’t as subtle and cautious as it was when I came in with Genograche.
Of course, Hibiki would have paid as much attention as possible, but… She had touched the alarm system concentrated with high-level magic and powerful forces.
The Union expedition team continued onwards, unaware that the wide-scale alert signal was being transmitted between the devils already residing in the barrier.
“The number of devils whom Jin-Wook has seen here has drastically decreased compared to that time. At that time, thousands of devils suddenly gathered in front of us and surrounded us.”
Thousands?
Then why were those all we that we had?
The number of devils that rushed out to stop us was only a few dozens.
While I was busy making sense of everything, Nate continued.
“Actually, I thought I was going to die then. There’s too much difference in numbers. Regardless, I didn’t want to get killed just like that, so I prepared to fight, but the moment I called my subordinates out…”
The situation turned upside down.
Nate summoned his subordinates, the undead, as usual.
At that moment, the devils, who were approaching them little by little, looked frightened and surprised and acted like they worshiped Nate.
It was hard for Nate to understand.
However, someone seemed to have a clue as to why.
– Indeed, I suppose it’s understandable.
In unison, we turned our heads towards the voice behind us.
“?”
Genograche, who was listening to our story while walking along, stepped in.
He asked Nate a question out of the blue instead of explaining.
“These guys must probably be the descendants of the Monarch of Evolution’s subordinates, aren’t they?”
Nate watched the atmosphere of the devils walking ahead of them and nodded.
“I think so. But these devils must have been stuck here for too long. It seemed like they no longer know what happened in the past. I mean, they do know, but should I say that there are a lot of things that are omitted?”
According to the stories passed down to the forest’s devils, they regarded themselves as a militant species excommunicated from the ‘blessed land.’
Nate continued.
“They’re obviously devils based on their looks, but they don’t seem to know that they’re part of the magic species.”
According to their perception of history, long ago, they served a great Monarch in a blessed land.
However, they waged war against the ‘devils’ that suddenly appeared and eventually lost, forcing them to be driven out to the forest and hide.
I sensed irony when I heard that part.
‘The natives who live outside the forest call the magic species the Devil, and these magic species regard the Awakened that drove them out as the Devil.’
The reason for hiding in such places, instead of the devils dominating them or leaving the woods and moving freely, was also related to the tale told by the seal aliens, the Lutresians, which were non-awakened and were much weaker than the magic species.
“They think that those devils should never know the fact that they’re still alive and surviving in here. They say that’s why they never get out of the cracked barrier unless it’s absolutely necessary.”
Genograche gave a bit more details.
“As you said, the passed-down story seems to be in a mess and is missing too much detail.”
He pointed at Nate and said.
– Somehow, I think they mistook you for the ‘Monarch of Resurrection.’ He was able to command the dead, too.
Nate tilted his head.
“The Monarch of Resurrection? I’ve never heard of that name before.”
It was the same for me.
“There’s one such title that came out of those devils. It’s awkward since it’s conveyed through interpretation magic, but they said something about a great warrior that controls the dead? They call me something like that.”
They must’ve remembered what his abilities were but had forgotten the title. The Monarch of Resurrection was one of the devils who the Monarch of Evolution ruled.
A monarch controlling a monarch?
– There was a reason behind that. I’ve already told you what power the Monarch of Evolution had, right?
The Mana Core naturally formed without being chosen by the System to become a user… Essentially, among those with Mana Core, some individuals developed special powers only they could use.
One such example was the Dragon Breath.
They called it abilities, which was the same as users’ Unique Skills.
The Monarch of Evolution’s ability was the gift to increase other people’s potential Mana and help them go beyond their limits.
– Even the Awakened beings that made a contract with the System rushed in to be that devil’s subordinate. Would it be any different for a Monarch? The Monarch of Ressurection was said to be able to manipulate more undead than before ever since he started serving him.
Nate nodded as if he had just understood it then.
“For these devils, the Monarch of Evolution is the god, and the Monarch of Resurrection must be about the level of an archangel, right?”
– … Why use such a metaphor out of all the ones you could’ve used? Anyway, I think it was passed down in a similar sense.
“No wonder they kept saying weird things to me.”
It seemed that through Hibiki’s help, Nate became somewhat civilized enough to not mess up by saying things such as ‘I’m not a devil, though?’
Since they worshipped him, my members most likely allowed them to keep doing that.
Nate returned to the story of the expedition team’s encounter with the forest dwellers.
“They invited us inside of this barrier. So we just followed the devils.”
They were treated as VIPs, and the expedition team had a serious discussion in bafflement.
The quest objective was to find traces of the Monarch.
But would they be qualified for Quest Completion only with that?
The Roheems reported their existence to the System and suggested converting the quest into a ‘devil hunting’ quest.
– What?!
Genograsche showed signs of discomfort all of a sudden.
However, Nate continued, saying that they opposed the suggestion.
“The magic species are living peacefully among themselves here. Why should the Awakened come all the way here to hunt? I felt it while observing them as well. They’re different from Dungeon monsters. They’re not feral beasts whose eyes burn of bloodlust and whose instincts scream for them to kill.”
While he talked, the long passage ended, and a huge underground space unfolded in front of us.
I spoke up in pure amazement.
“Was it this large-scaled?”
The underground city was wide enough to accommodate more than ten thousand people.
Contrary to my response, Genograche muttered disapprovingly.
– I can’t believe it wasn’t enough for the devils to be kicked out of the magic kingdom because of the System. They have to live in hiding underground like rats too… Damn it.
Nate pointed to the city.
“The one that governs this place… Using Earth’s term, the devil that acts as a mayor of this place is called ‘Knight’ by the residents.”
A Knight was originally the title of the devil that commanded the army under the Monarch.
The original owner of the golden armor thieved by Genograche was a Knight.
The word’s value had depreciated. At the moment, it seemed to be used as a title for the head of the administration.
“As the opinions between Roheems and Terrans collided and didn’t go along, Hibiki suggested an alternative. The traces usually refer to the items, skills, or magic-related information that the old being left behind, right? So all we had to do was focus on those things.”
When one found a clue about the unique abilities that the Monarch possessed, the System then exchanged and bought it with points.
It was then assumed to be redistributed in a form accessible to the Awakened contracted by the System.
“So we met the Knight and got some additional information about the old owner that created the barrier surrounding this city a long time ago and went off alone to fight off the invaders while keeping the residents hidden… We also tried to get clues about where the ‘Monarch’ had lied. They said that only the Knight knew about that. However, he refused to inform us about it.”
The Terrans insisted on persuading them more instead of fighting the friendly devils, and everyone decided to stay overnight in the city for that reason.
However, the Roheems attempted to kidnap the Knight while everyone was asleep.
It seemed their intention was to monopolize the System rewards instead of sharing them with humans.
“Us, and of course, the devils fought together, but the Knight was kidnapped in the end.”
Contrary to many Roheems dying, the Earthlings’ casualties were only one, thanks to Hibiki and Nate’s performance.
The problem was what happened next.
“If I were to do as I wished, I would’ve tracked the Roheem bastards right away, but I couldn’t.”
We soon saw the reason.
As we got closer to the accommodation of the Terrans, the disgusting smell stung our noses.
It’s a familiar smell.
“Isn’t this the smell of rotting corpses? Could it be…?”
Did someone else die in the meantime?
Nate shook his head.
“No, it’s not what Jin-Wook thinks.”
As I approached the door, I observed it closely with [The Successor’s Eyes].
Crack!
And I couldn’t help but grind my teeth because of the swelling anger.
Ten human Hunters were lying weakly.
The one who died was said to be temporarily sealed in the item, so the rest were definitely still alive.
Nevertheless, a terrible rotting stench was flowing out of their bodies.
I looked at the Mana Cores of the bedridden ones.
“… It’s a curse.”
It was a skill type that most Earthlings didn’t know before, but things had already changed.
Nate nodded his head.
“As soon as the fight ended, we noticed something wrong with them.”
The first one to fall was reported to be Hibiki.
“Looking at it, it seems like it’s a curse with a quite tricky activation condition. It makes me think that perhaps killing the colleagues of the skill holder may be the trigger. It’s because Hibiki, who had slain the most Roheem bastards, is in the worst state.”
I approached the bed he pointed at.
There, Hibiki laid in a ghastly shape.
There were evident signs of black rotting throughout her revealed skin.
When I saw it, sparks flew from my eyes, and blazing heat rose from my throat.
Hibiki barely managed to open her eyes.
“Oh… Guild Master!”
A weary voice.
I stared at the red Mana tangled in her Mana Core.
It was a combination of someone other than her own.
‘It’s a Unique Skill.’
It was similar to how the original Seo Jin-Wook was affected by the [Mercadius’ Seed].
The effect of the curse was to cause the body of the living to decay slowly.
Surely Nate must have been hit as well, but there was no sign of a curse on his body.
Could it be that his Unique Skill’s properties made him immune to it?
Well… Among Nate’s subskills, there was an ability that allowed him to turn his body into an undead. Understandably, such skills wouldn’t work for him.
I suppressed my wrath as much as I could.
“First of all, let’s make you feel better.”
I would just have to use the same method that got rid of the curse on my body.
I was going to open the [Door of Hope] and bring Iponia from Earth for a while.
“Revenge will come next.”
“Couldn’t it be that the Roheems have already returned to their dimension?”
I shook my head.
“The quest is yet to be completed. The Union headquarters thinks both Roheem and humans parties are missing. They were sure that you all were going to die if they left it be, so they haven’t contacted the Union yet.”
So they would be completely off guard.
I meant to crush piece by piece the entirety of their skulls while they were leisurely waiting, unaware of what’s on their way.

chapters.title: Chapter 181
chapters.content:
Trace of the Monarch (4)
*”Meeeow!”
The Iponia, Cat’s cry reverberated sorrowfully.
I brought it through the [Door of Hope].
“You’ll have to help me again this time.”
It had eaten up an enormous curse called the [Seed of Mercadius] and didn’t put anything near its mouth even if after we gave it a skill card because the seed kept it full for a good while.
However, it was starved a little at the time, and recently it started pestering for food again. Hibiki once told me that it didn’t even look at C-Class or lower skill cards, unlike before.
Of course, we couldn’t starve the Iponia just because the goal why we started to take care of it had been met.
Anyway, I owe it to Cat, and it was a bit weird to call it a reward, but I thought I would continue to take care of it.
It’s a pet that cost a lot to maintain, but it was nothing for me.
And unexpectedly enough, we got help from Iponia again today.
“Meeeeeow!”
A sad cry from Cat that I had never heard of before resonated in the underground city.
As soon as I placed it on the floor, it ran, approached Hibiki’s bed, and jumped up.
Then it crouched by Hibiki’s head and licked her hair nonstop.
It showed similar behavior to how cats groomed each other.
“Meeeow!”
As if it knew Hibiki was in bad condition, it looked at her with its eyes wide open.
And then as if it had reached a decision…
Hissss!
I didn’t even tell it to, but bright light began to linger in its eyes.
“Wait! You’ll get a stomachache if you eat it up that way.”
I hurriedly pulled up the god’s power.
That was because although it had nearly reached maturity, there weren’t only one or two curses to be removed that day.
As insurance in case of emergency, I brought out the power of the god of life, ‘Rom.‘
Whooong!
The fog-like divine power was released from the back of my hand, enveloping Cat.
The Iponia leaped through a few years to reach an age when it was in the most powerful stage in its life cycle.
Perhaps it’s because it had already experienced it before, but it didn’t even panic anymore.
The Iponia glared at Hibiki’s heart with the eyes of a predator in front of its prey.
The sharp light flashed in its eyes.
“Now, there you go. Eat it up!”
“Meeow!”
A blue wave spread from Cat’s eyes.
And it poured out toward the cursed Hibiki’s heart, her Mana Core.
As the curse itself wasn’t manifested in a similar living form as the [Seed of Mercadius], it didn’t put up fierce resistance as the seed did.
There was also no howling of the hunted beast.
Shhhhh!
It was almost too easy for the Iponia.
The red Mana pattern that surrounded Hibiki’s heart weakened evidently.
Then it slowly separated from the Core and fell off.
“Hisss!”
Cat hissed.
The moment the curse was completely separated and fell out of her body, it rushed toward the Mana agglomeration, which looked like a spider’s web or a vein due to its wavering shape.
It then released a much sharper and more precise attack than when it hunted my heart’s seed.
“It’s done!”
The red Mana was torn to pieces in the air.
Cat devoured the shredded curse without leaving a single piece.
“Meooow!”
It sat in a majestic position and wagged its tail after it succeeded in vanquishing its foe.
“It’s not time to be full yet.”
Following my instructions, Cat also began to eat the curse of the remaining people one by one.
It was literally an eat-all-you-can day.
“Ah, Guild Master!”
After the curse disappeared, I approached and cast a recovery spell.
The devils were shocked, seeing that the rotten portions that didn’t heal no matter how hard they tried had cleanly disappeared as if they never existed in the first place after the curse had been lifted.
The guild members looked at Iponia and me as if we were saviors, saying that they’ve suffered indescribably terrible pain.
Hibiki, who served as the leader of the Earthlings sent to finish the quest, apologized as soon as she regained her energy.
“… I’m sorry. I should have paid more attention.”
She walked toward me like she’s ashamed and bowed her head down.
I tapped her shoulder encouragingly.
It was absolutely not something for her to be sorry about.
“No, it’s hard to predict what kind of Unique Skills your opponent has. Furthermore, if they invisibly placed the curse during a fight, it would naturally be harder to counter.”
That was the case without the [The Successor’s Eyes].
On the other hand, at that moment, unlike her, there was someone who was expressing anger profusely.
“How dare those inferior bitches place a curse on my body!”
It was the dragon that tagged along to recharge everyone’s Mana, Euclid.
She expressed her terror and shame into anger. She spoke about falling helplessly to the doings of a race that couldn’t even reach her foot in terms of Mana.
For reference, because she hadn’t been able to maintain a polymorph until she was treated, she had been quarantined by a barrier, occupying an entire vacant lot in an underground city.
There was a reason why the devils put up a new barrier.
The terrible smell emitted by a dragon rotting alive… It was similar to hundreds of tons of rotten meat piled up, forming a mountain of decay.
“Now, calm down.”
The dragon, steaming and breathing fire to relieve her rage, returned to a bald elven shape through polymorphism.
I finally addressed everyone as a Guild Master.
“You’ve done great, everyone.”
eyes.
“I know. We still have blood to be paid back.”
One hunter was killed in the collision against the Roheems.
It was a pity.
“I’ll take care of the revenge and the rest of the quest. For now, all of you return to Earth and remain on stand by.”
I added words so they wouldn’t misunderstand.
“It doesn’t mean that I’m reprimanding you for failing the mission. As long as we know that the opponent’s Unique Skill is a curse, there is a risk of taking revenge with the same member composition. It’s not like the Iponia can indefinitely eat up the skill as well. I have to step up.”
The guild members agreed and went back one after another through the [Door of Hope].
The remains of the hunter that died were also recovered and carried away with them.
However, some Hunters insisted on staying despite my instructions.
They were Nate, Hibiki, and Euclid.
Nate and Hibiki, who took the role of leading the guild members, wanted to help me since they desired to see the responsibility through the end. Euclid didn’t care about any of that. She just wanted to take revenge against the disgusting apes.
Nate seemed immune to the decay curse, so I easily allowed it, but I contemplated about Hibiki and Euclid for a moment.
“Alright, I’ll allow it.”
But I agreed soon enough.
“Even if an emergency occurs, one person… plus dragon should be able to be taken care of by Cat.”
I looked at the two humans, a dragon, an alien animal that looked like a cat, and the devil that followed me.
“Well, let’s go return this disgrace by multitudes.”
*
In a forest far from the underground city of devils, a devastating scream resonated.
“Aaaargh!”
The man tied to the tree was a species leader called the “Knight” by the devils of the forest.
His thighs had already disappeared.
And the cut section was so tattered that it was difficult to look at.
Traces of cruel torture.
At that moment, the hand that was tormenting him was approaching again.
Tssssss!
“K-eeeeup!”
Fireball made from magic seared his groins.
However, the Knight stared at his opponent with fierce eyes, even as he vomited blood.
He snapped at the Roheem race that tortured him.
“Kill… Me! Whatever you do to me… I won’t tell you anything!”
The Roheems, who were in charge of torture, shook their heads as if it was unbelievable.
“Tough little bastard. I can’t believe he’s holding on so strong.”
Then one of the torturers turned his head and called someone.
“Hey! Trade places with me. I’m tired.”
“Okay, I’ll take over.”
The approaching being grumbled as he gathered Mana in his hands.
“Look, you probably think we’ll give you an easy death if you keep acting like that, but you’re mistaken. Do you know how many points we spent just to get here?”
The price of a Leap Ticket needed to enter a dimension not connected to any Gates was high.
Since it turned out like that, they had to get their money’s worth.
They were trying to find out where the “Monarch of Evolution” faced his end, a secret that only the Knight knew.
“Never… I will never tell you!”
“Is that so?”
The Roheem species laughed.
“I’m going to be a little different from the previous ones. Unlike them, I actually specialize in this.”
From his hand, sharp Mana debris fluctuated like a sandstorm.
“Now, I’m going to put this in your mouth from now on. And it will tear your gums, tongue, and mouth ceiling apart like sanding…”
The threat didn’t happen as the tormenter intended.
Crush!
It was because there was a sound of something hard breaking behind his back.
“What was that?”
The Roheem species member who was about to begin the torture turned his head urgently.
One of his colleagues was slowly falling, the head of which was nowhere to be found.
“Oh, damn it!”
The faces of the Roheem race who identified him were dismayed.
The one who just died was an Awakened who used a special curse with the Unique Skill.
“We’re being attacked!”
Soon the raiders appeared from the woods.
Seeing them, the Roheem muttered with a bewildered face.
“Human?!”
The Earthlings were supposed to die soon from rotten organs caused by the curse they inflicted upon them.
Since the Celestial Dragons Guild Master had stepped up, it became child’s play to track them down no matter how far they ran away.
Seo Jin-Wook, who showed his face in front of them without any plans to hide his identity, held the broken sword in his hand and approached silently.
Whooong!
The Mana was converted to divine power, and a bright light wrapped around the halved blade.
It soon manifested a light sword, eradicating any signs of imperfection.
Seo Jin-Wook spoke using a small voice, glaring at his prey with wrath and rage.
“Leave the one that I’m pointing at now, and slay the rest.”
The Roheems took out their weapons and spat out.
“Crazy bastards. You think five of you….”
Before he could even finish speaking, the five Earthlings began a frantic slaughter.
“K-argh!”
Screams resonated nonstop.
To prevent the kidnapped Knight from getting caught up, they avoided a wide-area attack and killed their foes by killing them one by one.
Seo Jin-Wook, of course, was the lead in the hunt.
Every time he swung his sword, one of the Roheems died.
One life for every motion. He displayed efficient movements.
A brief flash of his sword swiftly and unconditionally brought down death.
As ten people left for the underworld in an instant, the Roheems seemed to notice that something was wrong.
“N-no, wait. This is-!”
Genograche was also madly charging and cutting open Roheem necks, causing alien blood to coat him, and Nate’s zombie horde gnawed and tore Roheems by relentlessly attaching themselves to their targets.
Hibiki crushed the enemy by distorting gravity with a stern look on her face. Euclid, who stood beside her, also burned and torn the aliens using the spell she learned from Hibiki instead of focusing only on charging Mana as she used to.
The Roheems had been enveloped by terror and fear at that point.
“R-run!”
The Roheem, who shouted so, was also butchered by Seo Jin-Wook’s sword mercilessly.
His attack was more like a bombing than a cut or a stab.
When the lightsaber grazed, the target’s whole chest was blown away, and blood splattered down.
The Terran shouted in a wrathful voice.
“How dare you!”
– I’ll take this area.
Genograche chased the ones fleeing, launching his body as if he had no intention of letting any of their foes leave with their lives intact.
The magic species’ sword drew a sharp line, and the alien’s body was split apart vertically.
Those who Genograche touched had left a relatively “intact” body.
At least compared to the small pieces of ground meat left behind Seo Jin-Wook’s wake.
“How can a human being be such-!”
Someone shouted then.
They had finally recognized the identity of the new human being who was definitely not a part of the expedition team.
“Seo Jin-Wook! It’s Seo Jin-Wook!”
“What? No way! They surely said he was dispatched to another mission…!”
Listening to the hectically exchanged conversation, Seo Jin-Wook was able to see why they did it.
While he, who was considered the only threatening entity among the Earthlings, was absent, they meant to finish the job and destroy the evidence altogether.
However, Seo Jin-Wook finished his work faster than expected and had returned to Earth.
And he ran over right away to save his guild members.
“Aaaargh!”
When Seo Jin-Wook moved to where the Roheems were gathered, more than ten Awakened beings were torn apart as if a grenade exploded amid them.
Plo-plo-plop!
Intestines, flesh, and blood rained down all over his vicinity like a storm of ground corpses.
His sword no longer even needed to touch the bodies of the Roheems. A graze was enough for their flesh fragments to burst out.
“N-no way!”
Perhaps he was lucky. The Roheem that had only his leg cut crawled and desperately spread his distance.
However, the extended life span brought fortune lasted only a few seconds.
Crush!
Following the trajectory of the sword swung without looking in the direction, a sharp beam thundered through.
It penetrated the Roheem’s chest as he was crawling.
The movement of the alien, which was reaching out desperately with its heart pierced, stopped.
The Terran murmured lowly.
“I won’t miss.”
“K-aaargh!”
In the forest where the Knight’s screams used to echo, the slaughtered Roheem’s cries filled the atmosphere.
As they continued to exact vengeance, the forest’s fine humus soil became deeply stained with blood from the aliens.

chapters.title: Chapter 182
chapters.content:
Trace of the Monarch (5)
I left only one of my enemies alive as usual.
The last survivor shivered, having witnessed his colleagues dying instantaneously.
He looked at us with a face of despair and fear.
“Please, forgive me!”
Apparently, it wasn’t for his life that he was begging.
“This is not a matter of our species’ dimension, but a rogue act of each individual here. So, please, to the Union’s headquarters….”
It was a ridiculous thing to hear.
He was pleading to prevent the issue from developing into an interracial problem because he knew what kind of aftermath it would create if such agendas were to be relayed to the Union headquarters.
He just wanted us to end everything by killing them and punishing them.
“That’s funny.”
If they were worried about that, they shouldn’t have done that in the first place.
I glanced at Genograche, and he approached and held out the handle of his main body, the devil’s sword.
[Whisper of the Sword]
“Ahhh!”
That time, the brainwashing skill worked after so long when it didn’t, and thanks to it, we were able to get a confession quickly and efficiently.
When I heard the story, there was a reason why he, the sole survivor, was scared and blabbered.
It went without saying but behind the Roheem dispatched for the quest were the race’s political leaders and the Awakened beings’ Heads.
They sent the team to the dimension by buying expensive Leap Tickets because they were worried about their species’ future.
The Roheem people, like humans, didn’t have much Potential Mana Capacity.
They also showed keen interest in the traces left by the “Monarch of Evolution” for the same reason as me.
It could have been an opportunity to boost their power exponentially, after all.
“You didn’t want to share that treasure with the Terrans, the Earthlings.”
I thought they cheered when they saw that I wasn’t on the list of explorers sent by Earth.
And saying that it was the only chance they had, they tried to monopolize the Monarch’s traces.
“Okay, thank you for your confession.”
I turned my head after sealing him in an item that looked like a coffin.
The devil tied to a tree was rescued, and Hibiki’s healing magic and items had completely healed his wounds.
The Knight that represented the forest devils…
As I approached him, he wriggled with an uncomfortable expression.
“Ugh! What the hell!”
I belatedly understood why he was reacting like that.
“Oh, I see.”
I lowered the output of the divine power emitted by the Holy Sword.
He resisted the power of a god, not different than any other devils.
Then, as if the rock that was pressing down on his chest had been removed, the devil gave a sigh of relief.
While he was catching his breath, I looked interestingly at his face and exposed bare arms.
‘Tattoo?’
His skin was full of intricate shapes.
Nate explained as if he had noticed my gaze.
“They say it’s a tattoo that you have to get when you become the Knight in charge of representing the devils here. But even they themselves don’t know what it means. It seems like it’s a type of script because of the repetitions in the pattern…”
Among the ones present, Genograche and I knew the identity of that script.
Genograche clicked his tongue.
– You even forgot the ‘contract text’ that belongs to the devils?
I carefully examined the Knight’s body.
I observed that the text string wasn’t perfect. Grammar was wrong in some places, and there were broken letters as well.
“There must be some distortion or omission while it was being passed on to so many generations. I can’t read it like this.”
– Is that so?
Genograche also approached the Knight.
The Knight, who repeatedly thanked Nate and Hibiki for saving his life, as he was at least a bit familiar with them, turned his head again to the two of us.
Since he had witnessed the massacre that just transpired, it seemed that he was still sacred even if we were the saviors of his life. His eyes were even trembling.
But the moment Genograche took a step ahead of me and extended his head to read the text…
Whoooong!
“What?”
– Hmm?
The tattoo on the Knight’s skin began to glow.
And a strange change began that wasn’t normal for a common tattoo.
As if an earthworm was crawling on his skin or the text was alive, it began to wriggle.
White-flashing text strings were disassembled, recombined, and formed sentences. What happened afterward was…
“Huh? Huh?”
Nate gave off a baffled voice.
The Knight’s face was also dyed with shock, but his eyes were filled with awe beyond bafflement.
He seemed to know what the phenomenon was, but he didn’t expect to see it at that moment.
Soon, we all saw a curtain of letters falling out of the Knight’s body like light powder in the air.
I spoke.
“Now I can read it.”
Genograche mumbled in reply.
– This is a headache…. It used the entire skin of the devil as a ‘magic document?’
It was a kind of contract, based on the form of it.
In other words, the Knight’s body was used as a living contract.
The first to engrave such was probably the Monarch of Evolution they served.
Since then, whenever the Knight’s position was passed onto the next, they seemed to imitate the Monarch and inked the successor.
Each time, the contract’s magical effect was automatically passed on to the successor without their knowledge.
“However, it doesn’t seem like an approved contract, does it?”
The Knights only served as the paper for the original text of the contract. Nobody had placed their soul as collateral.
Genograsche read the first paragraph.
– You, a soul with comparable quality to the ‘Monarch.’ If you’re reading this, it means that my servant or his descendants are finally standing in front of the magic species, which are well qualified.
The more we read the words that followed, the clearer it became.
That was laid down for posterity by the Monarch of the distant past.
I could see why it was activated at that moment, of all times.
‘A soul that has the qualities of a Monarch…’
Genograche’s soul was sealed inside the devil’s sword at the moment, but he was also a Monarch, called the ‘Monarch of Massacre.’
‘It had reacted to Genograche.’
The sentences, which served as the preface of the contract, explained the Monarch of Evolution’s situation in the past.
– As I’m leaving this message, the Awakened beings controlled by the System are chasing me, and a battle seems inevitable. Considering the opponent’s combat force, running away no longer holds meaning. Many of my fellow kin have been sacrificed while we were fleeing across many dimensions. Now, there are only a few left.
The story about the ancestors of the devils living in the forest continued.
– Most of my Knight-level subordinates have mostly died, and many of those but ordinary citizens are injured and exhausted. Since it is futile even if we mobilize them to the battle, I instructed them to hide in this place for a while until the day that another Monarchial kin that would save them would appear.
But the savior didn’t seem to have appeared as fast as the Monarch expected.
– Soon, I will head alone on the battlefield. But I plan to be captured as the Awakened are after. They say the System gives more experience points when captured than when the magic species are killed. The reason is obvious.
The System used the kidnapped devils for
– We are the first race to open our eyes to the grace of Mana. We were the ones who created Mana Hearts and enlightened ourselves of our own powers before the System could even exist.
The first life of the successor’s soul after returning to the past was also of the devils.
– The System has been hunting us for some time past a certain point. If I were kidnapped like this, wouldn’t I be sealed, enslaved, or my Mana Heart… the Mana source they call the ‘Core,’ be taken out? And the System would imbue my powers in the skill cards and distribute them to the Awakened.
Awakened beings traded their old Unique Skills to the System to be copied in exchange for their Unique Skills’ evolution, but it was believed that the devils, who had no contract with the System, were robbed as if they were being gutted.
– My power being scattered to the Awakened must be prevented by any means. If the power to break through the limits of a species falls into their hands, those who follow the System will become stronger beyond control, and our kind will simply not be able to overcome it.
There was a heavy determination in the following sentence.
– But even if so, I can’t let my power, a blessing, disappear like this. Unfortunately, all the Monarch-class devils except me have already passed on at the time of this writing. That leaves me with no successor to inherit this power.
But he didn’t give up.
– But as time goes by, I believe that another qualified devil will appear, and I plan to leave an arrangement for that. Ask my servant that bears this ‘letter’ on his body. He will tell you where you must reach.
That’s all I could read for the moment.
I reviewed the contents with a serious expression.
‘It seems that he surely left something behind.’
It’s certainly something related to the Unique Skill that the Monarch of Evolution had.
But how could a race that wasn’t linked to the System pass on its Unique Skill to others?
“Ahh!”
While we were reading the letter, the Knight fell flat on his face as if he realized the situation.
The subject of his homage was Genograche.
He seemed to feel something with his senses unique to the devils.
“We have so far served him, the one who commands the corpses, thinking that he was the descendant of the late Monarch.”
He was referring to Nate.
The gaze toward the human youth scratching his head flowed back toward Genograche.
“But it seems the true ‘Monarch’ existed elsewhere.”
He trembled with emotions that overwhelmed him.
“It’s finally time to carry out the mission that had been passed down from one Knight to the next. Allow me to lead you to the promised land, you, who qualifies as a Monarch.”
He wanted to tell us the secret that he had kept shut despite having to bear the torture of the Roheems as a consequence.
Of course, there was no reason to refuse.
*
The place where the Monarch of Evolution’s life came to an end was said to be far away, which took more than a month on foot.
Indeed, it should have been distanced at least that much to ensure the hidden subordinates’ safety.
Of course, there was no reason to walk there since flying wasn’t difficult if I knew the direction and distance.
And where we finally reached, we saw the third barrier.
‘This can never be found without [The Successor’s Eyes], can it?’
There was no such thing as a crack again that time.
When we reached the great dome, the inscription on the Knight’s body shone once again.
And-
Shhh!
The barrier opened.
“This is the last place the Monarch hid in before his death.”
The Knight’s explanation followed.
Once upon a time, the quest to capture the Monarch of Evolution disappeared after he was considered deceased.
However, since the battle ended in a double defeat for both parties, the Awakened couldn’t know the truth behind the aftermath.
In fact, the Monarch did not die immediately after the fight ended and slaying all the Awakened.
However, knowing that death could not be avoided due to serious damage that he couldn’t recover from, he hid within the barrier that had been prepared in advance.
He was also said to have triggered a pre-implemented magic circle as well.
Whoooong!
Next, the sentences of light rising in the air continued the explanation.
An article with different content from what we just saw appeared.
– I could only think of one way to pass on my powers to future generations. Unlike those brought to Awaken by the System, our unique power, as we have been enlightened with our own strength, is engraved in our soul.
I thought it referred to a skill like [The Successor’s Eyes] that was imprinted on my soul even before the System began.
– At the last moment, I forcibly removed my soul from my body and sealed it in this crystal.
A transparent crystal was emitting subtle radiance in the interior space of the crystal barrier.
Upon contact, [The Successor’s Eyes] popped up a message.
[Crystal with Sealed Power (Rank: ???)]
– A crystal that has someone’s soul and power sealed within. The effect is unknown at this time.
The text string of light continued its explanation.
– However, one thing must be agreed upon by the being that gains possession of this. As you may have already noticed, this document is in the form of a contract. The successor who will inherit my power must enter into a contract with their soul as collateral.
What did the Monarch of Evolution set that arrangement for?
Why did he want to pass on his powers to future generations?
The answer to such a question was soon revealed.
– I speak to the devils of the future. If you absorb this crystal, not only will you command my soul as a whole, but you will also be able to use my unique power at your disposal. In return, perform for me the contractually bound agreement.
His request was literally something a ‘Monarch’ would do.
– I want you to save all of my citizens, all of them left in this world. Take them in as your people and let them live in a safe place where the slaves of the System cannot harm them.

chapters.title: Chapter 183
chapters.content:
Training Fight (1)
“The citizens… Does that mean saving the magic species of the forest left here?”
The letters of light continued to embroider the air.
– Magic species of the future. Upon accepting the contract, my soul, along with my power, will be absorbed by your Mana Heart. But you can be at ease. I will only continue to exist in there, and I won’t intervene with your mind at all. I, too, shall adhere to the agreements stated in this contract.
– Keep in mind that my power can only be transmitted to the soul of the contractor, in other words, to the body that contains your soul. This is to ensure that the contract will be fulfilled.
– This is the end of my letter. I don’t know how long it has been since my death or how many citizens will have remained when this document is read, but I think it’s a doable enough condition for you who has a monarch’s qualities.
I was lost in thought.
Would I be able to get the ability to increase the potential Mana in exchange for taking in the devils?
In fact, it didn’t matter much to me since I could just continue absorbing Cores, but for my colleagues and other Terrans, it was a very attractive option, considering it would strengthen their battle powers.
And it was tempting, considering it even as a successor, not as Seo Jin-Wook.
That was because it was an effective supplement to the situation where my current life’s destiny was certain to be Earth’s guardian.
It was then.
– Hey.
Genograche turned to look at me and continued.
– I can’t make this contract.
“Hmm?”
I thought for a moment and nodded.
“Oh, I see.”
The full text of the contract said the following.
The power would be transferred to the Mana Core of the body containing the spirit of the contractor.
But at that moment, Genograche’s soul was sealed in a sword.
He controlled the golden armor equipped with a Mana Core, but it was technically more of an empty shell without a soul.
And the power couldn’t be instilled in the sword that had no Core.
– I cannot fulfill that promise even if I make the contract with the Monarch of Evolution, either.
A separate contract with me subjugated him.
Therefore, realistically, it should be considered difficult to feed thousands of devils.
Genograche looked at me and made an unexpected proposal.
– So why don’t you perform the contract?
What?
Why did he recommend me to have all the good things all of a sudden?
“Why? Don’t tell me….”
Genograche explained, pointing to the shabby clothes worn by the Knight.
– It’s because it disgusts me to see descendants of the magic species hiding in a cave, like a ground rat, and trembling, not knowing when they’ll be hunted down.
He added a sentence as if he was embarrassed.
– Perhaps it would have been different if I wasn’t aware at all…
It was hard to believe that those words came from the one who killed so many devils in his lifetime.
“I didn’t know you were so close-knit, especially considering the past.”
Knowing what I was pointing out, he grumbled.
– You mean the devils I killed? There was a story to that that you’re unaware of.
Instead of giving me the full length of the story, he said something else.
– The power of the Monarch of Evolution is something that you desire as well. You have the ability to perform the contract, too. And these men are ready to follow orders and offer loyalty like a fanatic, worshipping you as a savior if they are taken in.
It certainly seemed to be that way.
I would lose the Mana Cores that I would spend to relocate all the devils on that planet to Earth through the [Door to Hope] and the cost of helping them settle on Earth.
On the other hand, I would gain thousands of Awakened individuals with an average S to SS Class level based on Earth’s standards and a special ability to evolve potential Mana.
No matter how hard I thought about it, it wouldn’t put me in red at all.
Although, there was one thing that bothered me.
“I don’t think anyone can get the power, seeing that contract is constantly mentioning Monarch-level devils.”
– You mean the qualification of the soul?
He said as if it was ridiculous.
– Are you seriously questioning that? Do you think your soul falls short of a monarchical demon? Or are you worried that the power attached to the soul will be particularly picky when it comes to the body and the genes?
Wel… the following was what a god once said about my soul:
‘It’s surprisingly tough and hard.’
“Well, the only way to find out is if we try it out.”
I wanted to know if I had the qualifications as well.
I reached out and grabbed the crystal.
Then, the laser-like text from the Knight’s skin faded and disappeared all at once.
We all waited in silence for what would happen next.
As we did so…
– You are…
That time, instead of a text message made of light coming up, the words rang directly in my mind.
The source was the crystal held in my hand.
‘It’s the sealed soul here.’
The Monarch of Evolution, who lost his body a long time ago and had been waiting for future generations to reach his hidden power, spoke to me directly.
– You are… Your flesh is not of the same kind as ours.
I answered back with what I had prepared because it was an expected reaction.
“However, I am determined to perform the terms of this contract faithfully. What do you say?”
The sealed soul seemed to ponder for a moment.
Then.
– … Thee. Your soul does not qualify as a Monarch.
What? That couldn’t be… the moment I almost asked back in that manner, he continued.
– You have a much greater and glorious soul than any Monarch I have ever met. Your soul is far superior beyond the bound framework of Monarchs.
Hmm?
– I’ve never experienced such a toughly polished soul. What a strange thing this is. But I can put my faith in it if it’s an entity like this.
Then the voice gave me a proposal.
– If one is qualified to guide my people, I must accept the frame that contains the spirit even if it does not belong to my kin. So, will you accept this contract?
I answered.
“Let the contract be signed.”
Paht!
Then a brilliant flash burst out, and the crystal I was holding disappeared as if it evaporated instantaneously.
But I was aware that it was being converted into pure energy and flowing into my body.
A unique red Maana pattern combined with the soul flowed into my heart then into the Core.
And after a beat, I saw a text string that was different from any other.
As the force was instilled in me, a phenomenon more than mere contact occurred, causing [The Successor’s Eyes] to react.
The explanation of the new skill came up.
[Ordeal for Transcendence (Rank: EX)]
– An ordeal will be given to the Awakened being designated by the user, and only they shall be able to recognize and be affected by it. The Awakened that has overcome it will have their potential Mana grow further and beyond their initial limits.
※ Be aware that only subjects that have completely activated and unlocked all of their potential Mana, leaving no potential Mana in reserve, can be affected by the skill.
※ If the subject fails to overcome the ordeal, the subject will be penalized for some time, not being able to cast this skill on the same subject. The penalty application period is subjective.
I mumbled inwardly.
‘So that’s how it works.’
If the Mana could continue to be increased without a limit, the Monarch of Evolution couldn’t have been defeated.
Not only did it have a condition to use it, but even if one overcame an ordeal, the content of which I wasn’t aware of, it would take time to give the next ordeal.
Until the subject converted all the newly acquired potential Mana to active Mana, that was.
‘And first of all, there would be no point in using it on me.’
As I continued to increase my potential Mana with Mana drain, it would never fall to zero and hit bottom.
That ability was solely for my companions.
A means of cultivating one’s power as a group.
“Then…”
After understanding what had happened through our conversation, the Knight laid his body flat on the floor.
Even though I already knew what his reply would be, I asked him.
“What do you say? Will you and your other kindred follow me?”
The answer was very quick.
At least a few words from the Monarch of Evolution that died after hiding them in that place must have remained intact.
When he found out that I was already ruling over another monarch and had him as a subordinate, even though I was not a devil, he gave me a title.
“I will you serve me with all my flesh, Great Monarch.”
“…”
Great Monarch. What was up with that sense of naming?
I clicked my tongue and prepared to return to Earth.
*
The immigration of the forest’s magic species to Earth proceeded faster than expected.
First of all, a temporary shelter for thousands of people already existed in Korea.
That was because the residences built for refugees who lost their homes due to dungeon breaks had become almost empty.
The Celestial Dragon Guild had expanded its influence in earnest, and I had begun to pay attention to prevent Gates from collapsing through the [Aurora of Stability], after all.
Thanks to that, instances of dungeon collapse in Korea and the whole world had almost disappeared. That was Earth’s current situation.
And after entering the Main Quest, as we interacted with the other world that I had laid the bridge to, we were supplied consistently with the technology and the materials of the alien world. The urban reconstruction speed had hastened incomparably to the past due to it.
“Guild Master, the Korean government has granted refugee status to all members of the magic species.”
“Thank you, Secretary Kim.”
All of them had already pledged their allegiance to me, the savior of the legend, and I had the magic species join the Celestial Dragon Guild.
Suddenly, our number increased by multitudes.
As a result, the edges of Secretary Kim’s lips had gone from ear to ear and didn’t seem to go down. Every time he passed by, I would often hear a melodic humming.
“These days, every day is like a dream. When I think about the past, I never thought a time like this would come…”
He sighed deeply as if it made him emotional.
It was understandable. After the Main Quest began, the Celestial Dragon had solidified its position as the world’s No. 1 guild, but it had another rapid growth once again.
As a result, the comparison between the Celestial Dragon and other guilds on the earth became meaningless, and even the media were already losing interest in ranking them.
“Guild Master, you became even more famous after the tutorial quest.”
We prevented the Gates from collapsing all around the world, negotiated directly with the high-ranking members of the Union, and virtually had sole control over the Tactical Fortresses, the deterrent to prevent the invasion from other worlds.
The Celestial Dragon’s influence wasn’t restricted within Korea, just as how my name had reached other worlds as well.
As a result, Earth’s greatest Awakened individuals also opted to gather at the Celestial Dragon, and the guild also swept away the Main Quest accessible to the Terrans.
Therefore, the EX-Class and System-Class items received as my guild members naturally monopolized quest rewards. The useless lower-class items were released to the market and passed on to other Hunters, which also improved Earth’s overall combat ability.
It was sort of a trickle-down effect.
Secretary Kim assured me.
“In this situation, if you, Guild Master, promises something… the Korean government will have no choice but to provide the best support by all aspect. I think the rest of the procedure will be completed quickly.”
The magic species settled in Korea at a surprising speed.
And like how other Union members didn’t attack Genograche just because he was a member of the magic species, nobody picked a fight or dared subjugate the others either.
In the eyes of the aliens, the forest devils were also my subordinates, after all.
Meanwhile, while the government took care of the complicated administrative procedures and the guild leaders, including Secretary Kim, took care of the household establishment, I focused on other things.
“Please conduct the experiment on me.”
The task to try out the newly acquired skill, [Ordeal for Transcendence (Rank: EX)].
Upon hearing the explanation, Hibiki was the first to raise her hand.
She, who was very bitter about falling helplessly to a curse recently, wanted to become stronger as soon as she could.
However, she had virtually stopped growing, having unlocked all the potential Mana amounting to a total of 50,000.
Knowing her feelings well, I nodded.
“I don’t know what kind of ordeal it is. Do you still want to proceed?”
Hibiki nodded with a glance of firm determination.
“Wasn’t it said that the Monarch of Evolution of the past had a lot of subordinates gathered around him since they wanted to be stronger? It wouldn’t have been so if it was dangerous enough to be too big of a risk.”
Her reasoning was sensical.
Eventually, she became the first test subject.
When I activated the skill, the red Mana lingered around her body.
Then only a few seconds had passed.
Thud!
“Hibiki!”
“Are you all right?”
She sat on the floor with her knees weakened.
The air surrounding us changed rapidly.
Nate was baffled and wiped off the sweat covering Hibiki’s face.
“What kind of sweat does-!”
At that moment…
“Blrgh!”
How could a person turn so worn out in such a short time?
With a blank look as if she had walked through the battlefield between life and death, she vomited blood on the floor.
“Cough!”
A rough cough followed.
Nate quickly pulled out a potion and fed it to her.
“What happened? What about the ordeal? Has it already started? Is this the ordeal?”
Unlike Nate, who was so anxious, I didn’t even have to ask Hibiki.
It was visible to me.
Her potential Mana nearly doubled compared to the before I used the skill.
The active Mana was about 50,000, remaining the same, but the potential Mana, which was zero, increased to 50,000 again.
The expansion of the vessel, which could nearly double in the future, had been achieved.
“You’ve overcome it?”
“… Yes!”
Barely composing herself, she confessed what she had witnessed.
Nate’s eyes widened.
“By your senses… You’re saying you’ve been fighting virtual enemies for years and years alone?”
It was fortunate that her mind didn’t collapse.

chapters.title: Chapter 184
chapters.content:
Training Fight (2)
When the skill effect was proved through Hibiki, the next to take on the challenge was Nate.
He asked Hibiki, as if he was afraid, digging into the details of the illusion. Including what was the hardest.
She replied.
“As soon as I entered, I knew that everything was just a fantasy- like a lucid dream. Since time flowed without eating, sleeping, or Mana running out after the battle started, I was aware that it wasn’t real. However, it was still hard despite that.”
She said that her mind and emotions felt worn out.
“And no matter how fake it is, if you fight and kill, isolated from the world for years… you’ll start feeling like your mind is burning out. Honestly, I think I was half crazy considering my condition just before I came back. When I came back to reality, that madness disappeared like a lie, but when I think about it, it still scares me a little.”
Hibiki said the scariest factor was that she felt like she was becoming a ghost immersed in slaughter and was drifting away from people she left behind in reality.
She suffered from the fear of not knowing how much longer one had to be locked up there.
When Nate heard that, he smiled and replied.
“Really?”
He turned his head and looked at me.
“If that’s the case, I think I’ll be fine, Jin-Wook. I’m ready. Cast it on me.”
“…”
His tone told me he didn’t worry about the side effects and pain Hibiki talked about.
He had an expression seemingly stating that he could endure years of suffering in isolation, away from the people in reality.
Perhaps that was the case since he’d already been through such a situation.
I asked him if he would really be okay because I was worried that it might provoke his trauma, but Nate didn’t seem to mind.
“Then, here I go.”
Eventually, I used the skill on him.
Similarly, it was merely a moment for us, but Nate’s face changed beyond recognition and showed a similar reaction to Hibiki.
“Cough!”
His knees bent and fell.
And Nate vomited blood on the floor.
“Cough! K-eup!”
The result of the ordeal was a success once again.
His potential had increased by more than 20,000.
But his appearance, though he assured that he would be fine, wasn’t ideal.
No, to be exact, it was as messed up as when Hibiki had just returned.
“My…”
Euclid assisted him.
Nate murmured.
“I thought I would be all right…”
He mumbled and vomited blood a few more times as he coughed.
“Being stuck somewhere for years, it’s something I’ve done before, so I thought I could do it again.”
He spoke in a solemn voice.
“But why is it so hard now? It wasn’t even real.”
He said that the situation of being left alone was more difficult than the endless fight.
Next, I also tried it on Genograche, but as he expected, the skill didn’t work.
I could only think of one reason.
The difference between him and others was that he had no soul in the body where his Mana Heart was.
‘That means it’s a skill that interacts with the soul.’
And the Dragon, Euclid, had only lived for hundreds of years and hadn’t yet activated all of her potential Mana, so she wasn’t a subject that I could use the skill on yet.
After experimenting with the most important people that way, I contacted the guild members.
Of course, I did it in secret.
Hunters, whose growth was blocked due to the vessels’ limitations they were born with, causing them to be obsessed with despair, had always existed.
Their classes were not important.
Whether it’s F or SSS class, the desire to be stronger was no different.
Since there would be nothing good resulting from the news leaking out to other dimensions, conducting experiments on Awakened beings while practicing extreme security resulted in more than a 90% success rate.
The failed cases also had something in common. Everything stopped when they explicitly expressed their willingness to “give up” in the virtual space.
Of course, those who gave up once had been given the penalty that they couldn’t challenge the ordeal for a long time.
It didn’t take long to experiment with all the applicants. From my point of view, I only used a little Mana using the skill, and the activation time and the duration of the skill were close to an instant.
All that remained for them was to individually activate the increased potential Mana and then prepare to challenge the ordeal again.
*
The impact of my newly learned skill on the guild was greater than I thought.
The Hunters who suffered due to their limits trained, hunted and went on quests incomparably harder than they used to when the road opened up for them.
In particular, the Hunters who had hit the plateau for years expressed their gratitude to me with tears or wailing as if it moved them even more than the others.
The greater the desire for strength, the more dramatic the reaction was.
Not all of the members were aware of it, but the changed atmosphere was noticeable and turned our guild even more lively.
Satisfied with the result, I visited the residence of the magic species.
They were also playing a part in the rising trend of our guild atmosphere lately.
“Guild Master, as instructed, limited to volunteers among the magic tribe, they are being dispatched to the dungeon Clears with the existing guild members. The response is very good. Both the humans and the magic species seem to be motivated.”
The devils couldn’t enter the dungeon Gates by themselves because they weren’t Awakened who agreed to a System contract.
Therefore, they entered after being recognized as a possession belonging to other guild members. The magic species, who were puzzled at first, also showed great performance by reawakening their unique fighting instincts when the hunt began.
“The magic species’ fierce combat style and persistent enthusiasm seem to have stimulated even the old guild members.”
And so they were keeping their heads straight and setting their motivation on fire.
Meanwhile, the magic species were shocked as well.
Having been isolated in the forest for a long time and living close to primitive life, they had forgotten most of the high-quality spells used by their ancestors.
However, although it was a skill that the System instilled into the Hunters conveniently, witnessing the advanced spells said to have made the magic species show expressions as if they had entered a new world.
However, the superior characteristics of the magic species were also revealed there.
“They are said to imitate A-Rank magic or so on the spot just by looking at it. At first, the power was a little weak, but… They say that as time goes by, they make perfect modifications based on their own liking.”
Ordinary human beings without [The Successor’s Eyes] couldn’t immediately imitate skills by glance alone.
They were Hunters who had become accustomed to the existing system wherein they became capable of using skills just by filling in the slots.
But the magic species were different.
The Mana-specialized race, which was used to creating and controlling spells on their own by observing their Mana Hearts (Core), used the Hunters’ spells as a reference to reproduce the results similarly.
Of course, it wasn’t a perfect copy like in the case of [The Successor’s Eyes], but it showed 40-50% efficacy. Due to individual characteristics and talents, they had different areas that they could copy, but that alone was outstanding.
That format wasn’t limited to magic but also applied to sword movements acquired in the form of skills.
The Terran Hunters felt as if their secrets were stripped bare.
“Hmm?”
As I approached the residence of the magic species, some individuals came to greet me.
But I didn’t notify them of the visit, did I?
“Oh, Great Monarch! You’ve come to such a humble place yourself…!”
They all lowered their bodies and paid their respect.
‘How did they know?’
The answer came from my Mana Core.
The Monarch of Evolution whose entire soul and power I absorbed had answered.
– A powerful divine power lives in your body. It’s natural for them to notice your presence when you’re this close. The sensitive ones among the citizens must have felt unpleasant from a while ago. For many reasons now, they are worshipping you, managing to interpret the foreignness as a sense of awe.
I carefully examined their living conditions since caring for the magic species to get along well on Earth was a contractual condition promised with my soul.
Of course, I instructed them to pay extra attention, so the guild members must have taken measures to make sure nothing was lacking.
As I wandered around, the magic species seemed confused by the gap between the touching emotion of a great leader who carried the Monarch’s will and the repulsion provided by the subtle divine power.
When I saw that, I suddenly wondered.
I murmured quietly.
“Why is it that only the magic species overreact to the divine power like this?”
– Hmm? Didn’t the subjugated Monarch-level devil explain it to you? He must be an ancient devil who was born much earlier than me.
“Weirdly, he never talks about such things in front of me.”
The following was how the Monarch of Evolution explained it.
– You must know we’re the oldest species in existence in this world.
“I know.”
– The early days of the material world were much more chaotic than now. In the species that appeared then, there were many mutagenic traits that are hard to find in the current era. In relation to that, we were born with the trait of objecting to divine power.
He continued.
– Thanks to that, we hadn’t been driven to extinction until now.
What?
“What do you mean?”
– Isn’t it true that the tribes that lived in our contemporaries were destroyed, and only we are the ones left? What do you think is the secret?
“Because you’re a race specialized in Mana?”
– There’s a more important reason. Because of our mutated nature, none of the devils serve a god.
That’s a given.
– Imagine the early environment of the material world. It hadn’t been long since the gods were exiled back then.
“Hmm.”
– They were in the early stages of losing their egos. Thanks to that, the gods were much more involved in the material world than they are now, and their influence was great. Therefore, the races that served a god at that time could perform near-miraculous phenomenons. They borrowed the ability to cut the sky, boil the sea, and move the stars.
“And such races are all extinct now, you mean?”
– Not because of the Red Gate. All of their civilizations collapsed or fought each other for internal reasons. The funny part is that the more individuals served in a dimension, the earlier they were destroyed. Do you know at which point these events started?
“Since the System made a bizarre move?”
I thought it started when the System suddenly changed its attitude, opening up numerous dungeons and properly starting the hunt against the magic species.
– Exactly.
At that point, I could recall the name of a certain species that would have provided a reason for their destruction.
Mercadius.
‘After the System joined hands with Mercadius and granted them a strange “breeding” ability, the first thing they did with its power was… to destroy races full of the gods’ touches?’
I was lost in thought when the terminal on my wrist rang.
Secretary Kim told me that a secret communication was being attempted from outer space.
“I should return.”
*
When I operated the telecommunication machine at home, Bachurka’s face took shape.
She announced the progress of the situation.
– The Roheems have agreed to accept all the terms and conditions we have offered in exchange for avoiding a forced withdrawal from the Union. In the future, they will have to pay the Terrans, to be precise, the organization you lead, a great amount of compensation for the damage they caused. Of course, the political organization behind the scenes also had to be stripped down from their place.
The agenda on Roheems seemed to be ending there.
I hastened the alien for the next story.
“What about Adgons?”
There was only one reason why she contacted me through secret communication, out of all the options, that day.
As a result of the investigation on the Adgon executive we handed over, the Union leadership, excluding the race, decided on the future actions.
– Six tribes of the command, excluding Adgon, have reached a secret agreement. We’re going to strike them soon.
It was the good news that I had been waiting for.
– However, we’re not going to attack their home dimension first. We have a method of hitting two birds with one stone to subdue Mercadius while securing evidence to add to the Adgon charges.
The hologram displayed planetary coordinates that existed in different dimensions.
Places that weren’t unfamiliar since Adam had already researched it before.
– These planets have something in common. Even though they’re all planets that aren’t the Adgons’ parent dimension, the Adgons occupy it and block access to other species, and no native inhabitants remain there.
She also mentioned another common factor.
The Adgons’ security for the planets had risen to a very high level ever since the resurrection of Igras-Sho’s eighth leg.
– We have testimony and evidence secured that something similar to the fragments of the magical god you, Seo Jin-Wook, liberated may be sealed in those planets.
Of course, attacking those places one by one was meaningless.
It would only be like giving the Adgons time to prepare.
The Union intended to carry out a joint assault operation at those target points and take complete control all at once.
That was a declaration of war against the Adgons.
– There’s a reason I contacted you directly this time, not through the Earth’s government agency.
She gazed at me.
– This operation should be carried out without the Adgons knowing it. We have to keep it with maximum confidentiality. And I want you, Seo Jin-Wook, to help us, too. I’m asking you because I know your skills are already superior to the best of the elite warriors of the Union.
I looked at the planets that came up in the hologram.
“You’re asking me to join the squad that’s assaulting one of them, right?”
– Yes, we will leave your target to your wishes.
At that moment-
Shhh!
The broken sword on my waist rose in the air and pointed in one direction.
It was at an angle that pinpointed one of the planets shown in the hologram.
I laughed bitterly at the scene.
“I think a god has already chosen for me.”
The beginning of a pan-dimensional counterattack against the Adgons was just around the corner.

chapters.title: Chapter 185
chapters.content:
Training Fight (3)
The route of the assault planned by the Union command, excluding the Adgons, was quite roundabout.
They planned to dispatch thousands of meticulously picked Awakened into a planet each time, but there was not enough stock of Leap Tickets to move them all at once.
Since they didn’t have such an item, naturally, they had to move through the dungeon Gates.
However, the problem was that the Adgons, who strengthened the planet’s security measure, had already expected that.
Thus, they concentrated the Adgon forces deployed at each target around the Gates.
If the Union forces entered the portals in the usual manner, they would be destroyed by revealing themselves to the lines of enemy fire.
– So, we decided to move through an open Gate on another planet at the target dimension. The plan is to fly back to the target planet from there.
The ruined planets and dimensions controlled by the Adgons were very old by objective standards.
Therefore, most of the time, the species that previously lived there expanded their territory by creating colonies on different planets before their destruction.
And since the planets used to have residents, Dungeon Gates or Red Gates opened in its atmosphere as well.
– Since there are no longer inhabitants, most of the Gates have collapsed, but the remaining ones can be used as a pathway.
Listening to the story that followed, it was a bigger plan than I thought.
The Union planned to move various materials and parts through the Gates of the wrong planet and build a huge spacecraft there that could carry thousands of individuals.
And then we were to get on board and sail over to the target planet.
But…
I pointed out that there was something unclear.
“So, how long would that take?”
Bachurka spoke with a shadow cast on her face.
– That’s the problem. It varies slightly from dimension to dimension, but it is expected to take at least three months based on Earth’s time.
“That’s too slow.”
It had already been more than two months since Adgon prisoner’s handover to the Union was done.
Even if I were to consider that the delay so far was inevitable because they were trying to secure testimony and evidence and locate the target planet…
It would still take another three months for everything to be completed.
That’s almost half a year wasted.
“Will you be able to prepare as covertly as you are now for three months? What if the Adgosn notices?”
– We will only have to do our best. There’s no other way at this point.
I pondered for a while and finally made up my mind.
It was the Union’s goal to strike the Adgons, but above all, it was a stepping stone needed for my long-cherished desire.
The fragment of the god that they hid…To free the things that corresponded to Igras-Sho’s leg was also a duty that I had to fulfill to get rid of Mercadius.
With that in mind, I decided to disclose what I had kept away from the Union so far.
“Let’s change the method.”
– What do you mean?
After the tutorial quest and having entered the Main Quest…
When I was invited to go to another dimension or visit the Union Headquarters, despite the fact that I had a much better method, I used the ‘invitation,’ in other words, the teleport scroll bundles they sent, instead.
I tore a scroll, moved to the front of the Gate, crossed it, ripped another scroll again, and repeated the process until I reached the destination.
That was because I didn’t want to let them know that I had the [Door to Hope].
If nobody could observe our movement routes, for example, when sending the Celestial Dragon Guild members to a Gateless dimension, we pretended to use a ‘Leap Ticket’ but really sent them through the [Door of Hope]. Other than that, we moved similarly to others.
‘Now that we have found a common enemy called the Adgons…’
The enemy’s identity within the Union had been identified. The time was right to disclose it to our allies, whom I had to work together with to destroy our target.
I told Bachurka about it.
– Is it true? Do you have such an item?!
“Yes, I haven’t used it properly until now because the consumption of Mana Core is great when moving through dimensions. But I think the Union can procure as many Cores as the operation would require. Cores are a much lower price than the experience points you’ll spend on Leap Tickets.”
– Of course! That’s great. A lot of holes in our plans can be covered that way!
*
Due to my initiative, the scheduled date of the assault had been shortened by more than two months.
A total of five planets have been targeted.
The Union’s Awakened units were divided into five groups, and not all of them gathered in one place before the assault.
It was to reduce the chances of catching the Adgons’ attention as much as possible.
I stood in front of the troops who were aiming for one of the planets.
“Then, I’ll open the door.”
It felt like the air was being pulled tightly because of the tension.
Despite being selected as the best at each dimension, there was solemnity in their eyes, perhaps because they knew the importance of the mission.
A war that would be the key to exterminating a race with horrible mental control… a race that could destroy innumerable dimensions if left unchecked.
A war to strengthen the influence of the exiled gods.
Whoooooong!
The ring on my finger turned into a hoop, expanding its shape.
The moment the space inside the frame was filled with cold light…
– Please enter the coordinates.
Theoretically speaking, the most efficient way was to open the door right in front of the black hole where the fragment of the god was sealed.
However, as if the Adgon people had been prepared for the small percentage of intruders that might be sent through Dimensional Leap Ticket, they had covered the black hole with an infrastructure.
It was confirmed in advance that a portal couldn’t be deployed to its proximity because of the artifacts installed in it.
Therefore, I had secured the coordinates of the nearest possible location to the black hole that the influence of any artifact hadn’t reached.
– Coordinate verification complete.
The enormous amount of Mana Core provided by the Union had been absorbed, so all that remained was to charge.
I nodded, looking at the commander.
Then the person responsible for the assault shouted in a heavy and sharp voice.
“All troops, forward!”
Awakened aliens ran in a row into the blue Gate.
I couldn’t afford to relax even after the last individual threw himself inside.
The news that a battle had begun on that planet would be delivered to the Adgons’ mother dimension. It wouldn’t take long for it to the other worlds.
I changed the coordinates inserted in the [Door of Hope] and then appeared in front of the other waiting troops, doing the same thing repeatedly.
And finally, the fifth one.
The troops would be moving in with me from that point on.
“I’ll now open it.”
Those mobilized from Earth for that operation were Genograche and me, only the two of us.
Only those who met the minimum level of force required for the operation were selected.
After everyone rushed to the door, I threw myself inside the last.
The blue light surrounded me.
Thanks to having completed entering the destination’s coordinates in advance, I immediately appeared at the destination without the artificial intelligence having to ask me questions.
With a strange sky surrounding me, the tearing wind struck my body.
*
The Union’s planned assault structure was fully predictable for the Adgons as well.
The strongest defense facilities around the black hole were all aimed at high altitudes because they thought they would approach it either by spaceship outside the atmosphere or through a Gate.
Likewise, their fortified structures aiming beyond the horizon were also strengthened to prevent enemies approaching from the ground through the Gate.
Nevertheless, a network of weapons with relatively weak firepower was installed against the Awakened transmitted from close range via Leap Tickets.
There was a reason for it. They knew that regardless of race, there was a limit to the experience points that the Union could mobilize at once for Leap Tickets.
